title: How to Calculate Parcel Slope and Screen Developable Land
description: Compare a 3-foot lidar grid with a 30-foot average and USGS 3DEP. See how resolution changes acres under a slope cutoff and download the source data.
coverAlt: The same 19.74-acre parcel on 2022 aerial imagery. A 3-foot lidar grid shows 16.28 acres at or below 5% slope. Averaging the same elevations to a 30-foot grid shows 19.74 acres at or below 5%.
coverCaption: One elevation source and the same parcel and cutoff in both panels. Orange cells exceed 5% on the native grid. Aerial imagery is from USDA NAIP.
intro: To calculate how much land meets a slope cutoff, derive slope from a bare-earth elevation model and measure the qualifying area inside the parcel. Save the resolution, acquisition dates, cutoff, and largest adjoining area. On a 19.74-acre Oregon parcel, 16.28 acres met an illustrative 5% cutoff on a 3-foot lidar grid. Averaging the same source onto a 30-foot grid increased that estimate to 19.74 acres.
takeaways: Use lidar-derived bare-earth elevation for slope. Keep dated aerial imagery alongside it to review roads, cover, and visible changes.
Calculate slope on elevation data that extend beyond the parcel, then clip the result. Measure the actual overlap of cells along the boundary.
Report the combined qualifying acreage and the largest adjoining area. Carry the elevation source and uncertainty into any layout or grading review.

blocks.text: The study uses the current Marion County polygon for tax lot 091W04B001000 near Stayton. Oregon’s DOGAMI Stayton quadrangle includes a 3-foot bare-earth grid from the 2008–2009 Willamette Valley acquisition. We averaged complete 10-by-10 blocks from that grid to create the 30-foot comparison, then calculated slope on both. This tests what happened when we changed the grid size while using the same original elevations.

blocks.text: At 5%, the total estimate grew by 3.46 acres after averaging the fine grid. The largest group of qualifying cells that share an edge grew from 13.05 to 19.74 acres. For a buyer trying to fit a 15-acre footprint, the fine grid would prompt a closer review of where flatter ground adjoins. The raster figures describe slope alone. Utilities, access, drainage, wetlands and layout still matter.

The USGS product is a separately published elevation grid. Its cells measured about 7.32 metres east to west and 10.29 metres north to south at this site. The 19.65-acre result at 5% is useful for an initial screen. Changes in source, processing or grid alignment can also affect comparisons between the USGS and Oregon products.

sections.heading: How do I calculate slope percentage and acreage from a DEM?

blocks.text: Download a bare-earth digital elevation model, or DEM, for the parcel and surrounding ground. Use the full buffered grid to estimate slope and apply the boundary afterward. Horn’s method uses a 3-by-3 group of cells, so clipping elevation first can leave gaps or alter the estimate around the edge.

Slope in percent is 100 times the rise divided by the horizontal run. For a raster, estimate the gradients east to west and north to south and combine their magnitude. Match horizontal distance and elevation units. On a latitude and longitude grid, measure the east-to-west and north-to-south cell spacing in metres at the site. A 5% grade is about 2.86 degrees.

Clip eligible cells to the parcel and sum the area of the intersections in an equal-area projection. Use a proportional weight for cells crossed by the lot boundary. Check that the clipped cells cover the entire lot and report any missing elevation coverage. For one connected-area estimate, count cells that share an edge and report the largest group by acreage.

sections.heading: How should I compare lidar and aerial imagery dates?

blocks.text: The Oregon lidar delivery used for this lot lists a 2008–2009 acquisition range, NAVD88 elevations in international feet and the Geoid03 model. The USGS tile has a 2025 publication date and NAVD88 elevations in metres. A tile publication date can be newer than the underlying surveys. Check acquisition, vertical datum, units and surface type before comparing elevations across sources.

The 2020 and 2022 USDA aerials use the same mapped footprint. The central field looks greener and the field tracks are more distinct in the 2020 image. Treat those as visual observations and check acquisition conditions before interpreting them. Use comparable elevation surveys to investigate a change in ground height.

sections.heading: What should a slope data API return for site selection?

blocks.text: Invariant Earth’s public field catalog documents point elevation and point slope, including how the 3DEP tile supports the slope calculation. For a parcel-wide screen, keep the boundary identifier, elevation product, capture and publication dates where available, grid spacing, slope units and cutoff. Return total qualifying acreage and the largest adjoining area with the calculation method.

Align the slope cutoff with the intended building, yard, road or solar layout. Have the design team check candidate areas against a current survey, grading plan and the project’s drainage and geotechnical requirements.

faqs.question: How do I find slope data for a property?
faqs.answer: Retrieve the parcel boundary and look up bare-earth elevation in the USGS National Map or the state lidar archive. Record the grid resolution and source date, calculate slope on a buffered window, then measure the results inside the parcel.

faqs.question: Can USGS 10-metre terrain data show whether an entire parcel is flat?
faqs.answer: It can support a regional screen. Check finer lidar where service roads, banks or small drainage features could affect the layout. In the Stayton test, 19.65 acres met a 5% cutoff on the USGS grid and 16.28 acres met it on the native 3-foot grid.

faqs.question: What is the difference between slope in degrees and percent grade?
faqs.answer: Percent grade is 100 times the tangent of the slope angle. A slope of 5 degrees is about 8.75% grade. A 5% grade is about 2.86 degrees.

title: How to Check a Property for Wetlands and Hydric Soils
description: Use wetlands maps, hydric soils, and a Corps determination to screen land for development. Download the parcel and soil data from a real Oregon case.
coverAlt: Aerial map of tax lot 1000 near Stayton, Oregon. The 19.74-acre lot has zero mapped National Wetlands Inventory acres and overlaps a hydric soil map unit by 1.76 acres. A separate Corps record describes Wetland 4 as 1.87 acres.
coverCaption: The county lot is outlined in cream, the hydric soil map unit is shaded gold within the lot, and the National Wetlands Inventory is in blue. Sources include USDA NAIP 2022 aerial imagery, Marion County GIS, USFWS, NRCS, and the Corps.
intro: Start with the current parcel boundary and the area the project would disturb, including access and utility routes. Overlay the National Wetlands Inventory, local wetland inventories, and USDA soil polygons. Then check for a field delineation and federal or state decisions that cover the work area. On a 19.74-acre lot near Stayton, Oregon, the federal inventory had zero overlap. A USDA map unit with hydric soil components covered 1.76 acres of the lot, and a Corps record separately described a 1.87-acre wetland on the east side.
takeaways: Clip inventory and soil polygons to the parcel or proposed disturbance boundary before reporting acreage. Keep each layer’s dates and scope with the result.
Hydric soil components flag places to investigate. A map unit’s representative component percentages cannot locate individual soils or delineate a wetland.
Check the field delineation and the agency review boundary before using an acreage figure in a layout, closing condition, or permit estimate.

Set the desktop screening footprint. Use a survey or legal description to resolve boundary disputes.

Work with the relevant agencies to determine which approvals the proposed grading, fill and crossings require.

blocks.text: For acreage, use a suitable equal-area projection, clip the layers to the review boundary, and dissolve overlaps within each layer. Keep mapped wetland acres, soil map-unit acres, and independently verified field acres in separate columns. A wetland polygon’s full acreage can include land outside your property.

blocks.text: The current Marion County boundary for lot 091W04B001000, abbreviated 091W04B01000 on the Corps map, measures 19.74 acres in our equal-area GIS calculation. We checked that polygon against the National Wetlands Inventory and SSURGO on November 23, 2026. The Corps made its determination for a separate 60.9-acre review area that included portions of multiple tax lots.

A field crew still has to locate soil conditions and any wetland edge within it. Our download includes the county geometry, the nearby inventory polygons, the clipped soil map units, and the separate Corps findings.

sections.heading: What does an approved jurisdictional determination tell a buyer?

blocks.text: The Corps’ January 12, 2026 determination NWP-2025-00423 describes four wetlands totaling 8.72 acres by the individual sizes it reports. It classifies Wetlands 3 and 4, totaling 3.91 acres, as jurisdictional under Section 404. It classifies Wetlands 1 and 2, totaling 4.81 acres, as non-jurisdictional in that determination. The Corps says Wetlands 3 and 4 abut Ditch 1, which it also determined to be jurisdictional.

The Corps wrote that it did not find Ditch 1 in either the National Wetlands Inventory or the National Hydrography Dataset consulted for the review. The memo gives its length as 2,359 linear feet. The map’s red Corps annotation gives 2,395 linear feet. Use the same jurisdiction finding in the record, then reconcile the governing geometry and length before estimating crossing impacts or mitigation quantities.

Check Oregon’s state process separately for work near wetlands and waters. The Department of State Lands describes its own determination, delineation review, and removal-fill permit process. The federal memo gives federal findings for the stated review area. The project’s grading and crossings, along with applicable state and local requirements, determine the next review steps.

sections.heading: How should a wetlands data API handle parcel screening?

blocks.text: Invariant Earth’s field catalog documents point-level checks for whether the point intersects an NWI polygon, distance to the nearest mapped wetland within 500 metres, and the SSURGO soil map-unit name and dominant-component drainage class. For parcel acreage, use the parcel and source polygons and calculate the intersection. The catalog’s wetland acreage represents the full selected inventory polygon.

In a GIS export or API response, retain the asset ID, boundary source, retrieval date, layer vintage where available, acres of intersection, and whether the provider returned data for the entire work area. Record the field delineation and any agency decision under their own identifiers. Use the result to decide where to commission fieldwork, check access or utilities, or revise the grading plan before pricing the site.

faqs.question: How do I find out if my land has wetlands?
faqs.answer: Check the National Wetlands Inventory and state or local wetland maps against the parcel and work area. Review soil and site conditions, then ask the appropriate agency or qualified consultant about a field delineation if the project could affect wetlands or waters.

faqs.question: Does a blank National Wetlands Inventory map mean the site is clear?
faqs.answer: A blank map or zero intersection means the particular inventory has no mapped polygon at that location. Inventory methods can miss resources. Site conditions, field delineation, and any applicable agency decisions still matter for development.

faqs.question: How do I calculate acres of mapped wetlands on a parcel?
faqs.answer: Retrieve the parcel and inventory polygons, project both to a suitable equal-area coordinate system, dissolve duplicate or overlapping inventory polygons, and measure the intersection with the parcel. Save the input vintages and the analysis boundary.

title: Census Tract Housing Vacancy and Rent Burden Data
description: Find Census tract vacancy and rent burden in ACS tables B25002 and B25070. Compare changing boundaries and calculate margins of error with a worked Austin example.
coverAlt: Two maps of the same part of Travis County. Tract 11 in the first map is split into tracts 11.01, 11.02 and 11.03 in the second. Estimated vacancy falls from 19.65% to 9.93% on the combined footprint.
coverCaption: The two maps use the same scale and footprint. Census TIGER/Line boundaries and American Community Survey table B25002.
intro: Use American Community Survey table B25002 for total and vacant housing units and table B25070 for the share of renter households spending at least 30% of their income on gross rent. To compare two periods, put both estimates on the same tract footprint and carry the survey’s uncertainty through the calculation. In an Austin-area example, the estimated share of housing units that were vacant fell from 19.65% to 9.93%. The evidence was too imprecise to tell whether rent burden rose or fell.
takeaways: Join ACS estimates to the tract identifiers and boundaries for their release year. Use the Census relationship file to match older and newer tract footprints.
Add the underlying counts before calculating a rate. Use the same calculation for each of the Census Bureau’s 80 variance replicates to estimate uncertainty.
For a planning memo or market comparison, report the survey period, denominator, geographic footprint and margin of error alongside each estimate.

sections.heading: Where can I download Census tract vacancy and rent burden data?

rows: Share of housing units vacant
B25002, line 003 divided by line 001
The share of all housing units classified as vacant, including seasonal units and other vacancies.
Share of renters spending at least 30% of income on gross rent
B25070, sum lines 007 through 010. Divide by line 001 minus line 011.
The share of renter-occupied housing units for which the gross-rent-to-income ratio can be computed and reaches the cutoff.

blocks.text: Use the five-year detailed tables at summary level 140 for tract estimates. The detailed-table downloads supply published counts and margins of error. The variance replicate archives include the additional values needed to calculate margins for derived rates and groups of tracts. Keep the 11-digit GEOID as text so a leading zero survives the join.

sections.heading: How do I compare housing data after a census tract splits?

blocks.text: Check the tract vintages before you match identifiers. The 2015–2019 ACS uses 2010 Census tracts, and the 2020–2024 ACS uses 2020 Census tracts with selected updates. The Census relationship file lists how older and newer tracts overlap, with separate land and water areas.

Old Tract 11 in Travis County, Texas (48453001100) split into tracts 11.01, 11.02 and 11.03. The Census relationship file assigns all 2,437,645 m² of land and 239,536 m² of water in the old tract to those three and shows that each successor sits wholly within the old footprint. Add the three 2020–2024 counts before you calculate the newer rates.

For a partial overlap, build a common geography from available finer-area counts or use a documented allocation method suited to the measure. The crosswalk gives an area of overlap. An area share alone cannot tell you what fraction of residents or housing units lived in that overlap.

sections.heading: What changed in Travis County’s former Tract 11?

blocks.text: The combined area had an estimated 5,715 housing units in 2015–2019 and 7,172 in 2020–2024. Estimated vacancies fell from 1,123 to 712 while housing stock grew. The change in the vacancy share excludes zero at the 90% confidence level. The change in the count of vacant units is less certain.

blocks.text: For rent burden, the estimated counts were 950 of 2,944 eligible renter households in the earlier period and 1,175 of 3,835 in the later period. The change in the share has an approximate 90% interval from a decline of 12.74 percentage points to an increase of 9.48 points. A planner can document the estimated rise in housing stock and lower vacancy share while recording the rent burden trend as indeterminate.

sections.heading: How do I calculate the margin of error for a combined tract?

blocks.text: For each period, calculate the result from the published counts. Repeat the entire calculation for each of the 80 Census variance replicates, including the sums and division. Subtract the published-count result from each replicate result, square the differences, sum them and multiply by 4/80. The square root is the standard error. Multiply it by 1.645 for the 90% margin of error.

For a change between nonoverlapping periods, take the square root of the sum of the two squared margins. This gives an approximate 90% margin for the difference. If the resulting interval includes zero, report that the survey cannot establish a direction for the change. For near-zero or fully saturated rates, and for replicate denominators of zero, consult the Census Bureau’s special-case guidance.

sections.heading: What belongs in a housing data API response?

blocks.text: For address-based analysis, Invariant Earth’s field catalog documents a tract identifier and tract-level fields for occupied units, median home value and owner occupancy. Keep the vintage shown for each field with the response. For this historical comparison, join the two ACS releases and the Census geographic crosswalk, then store the numerator, denominator, margin and original source version with each derived rate.

Housing planners can use the comparison to decide which neighborhoods need a closer look. Developers and market analysts can use it alongside dated leasing data when evaluating current supply. For a measure of units available for rent, check vacancy status in B25004 and the date of any listing or inventory feed.

faqs.question: How do I get housing vacancy by census tract?
faqs.answer: Download ACS five-year detailed table B25002 at tract level. Divide vacant units on line 003 by total housing units on line 001. Retain the survey period and calculate the margin for the ratio.

faqs.question: Which Census table measures rent burden?
faqs.answer: In ACS table B25070, add the four categories starting at 30.0% of gross rent as a share of household income. Divide by the total renter-occupied units in the table after excluding the Not computed category.

faqs.question: Is the ACS share of vacant housing the same as the rental vacancy rate?
faqs.answer: The overall vacancy share includes all vacant housing units. For a rental market measure, use a definition that isolates units offered for rent and the corresponding rental inventory. Table B25004 breaks vacancies down by status.

title: Texas Data Center Tax Incentives and Property Tax Abatements
description: Compare Texas data center sales tax exemptions with a signed Fort Worth property tax abatement. Verify tax bases, eligibility, deadlines, and actual credits.
coverAlt: Three separate evidence records for a data center tax review. Fort Worth’s signed agreement sets the local city rate, Tarrant County groups several tax accounts, and the Texas Comptroller certifies qualifying purchases.
coverCaption: A property tax agreement, an appraisal district or county tax record, and a purchase exemption answer different questions about a project’s costs.
intro: Texas data center incentives can affect the annual property tax bill and the sales tax charged on eligible purchases. Start with the signed agreement for the affected taxing unit and the Comptroller’s certification for the facility and purchaser. Fort Worth’s signed 2019 Winner LLC expansion agreement set a 20% city abatement for tax year 2022 on specified taxes, subject to investment and completion evidence. That city agreement and the state sales tax program have separate requirements.
takeaways: For a local abatement, record the taxing unit, affected property, base year, covered tax years, conditions, and any remedy for missed commitments.
For a Texas sales tax exemption, identify the statutory section, facility certification, purchaser registration, and eligible cost items.
For underwriting, separate the signed rate and the county’s reported actuals. Tarrant County reports Winner LLC’s combined amounts without assigning the actual credit to the 2019 expansion.

rows: Chapter 312 property tax abatement
The property and tax years a city or county agreed to abate, with performance conditions.
Signed agreement and amendments, legal description or account IDs, applicable taxing unit and tax year, appraisal and tax bill.

Any separately negotiated grant or rebate and the documented basis for payment.

Texas data center sales tax exemption

Comptroller certification date, facility and purchaser registration numbers, Form 01-929, and invoices that identify the qualified costs.

blocks.text: Search the Comptroller’s local agreement database by jurisdiction and legal entity, then pull the controlling agreement and any amendments from the municipality or county. Search the appraisal district and collector records for the property tax account. Keep a credit against assessed property and a separate economic development payment in separate lines of the pro forma.

sections.heading: What did the signed Fort Worth expansion agreement cover?

blocks.text: Fort Worth City Secretary Contract 52160 was signed by Winner LLC on April 8, 2019, and by the city on April 10, 2019. For 2022 it set a 20% abatement on city real property taxes attributable to the increase over 2019 values and on city taxes on qualifying new tangible personal property. The contract cites the separate city economic development agreement, Contract 46728 as amended. Read each agreement against the land and work it covers.

The city required a Certificate of Completion for the real and personal property commitments. The signed agreement set baseline thresholds of $50 million of construction cost and $100 million of qualifying new tangible personal property cost, with defined adjustments requiring written approval. It reduced the rate to 10% when the company missed the commitment to spend 15% of construction costs with certified minority- or woman-owned businesses. Section 7.11 describes recovery of city taxes in the event of termination for failure to obtain the completion certificate.

Tarrant County’s separate report lists order 130032 with maximum rates of 60% for the county and 40% for the hospital district, a ten-year term, and a planned 2022 start. Its February 12, 2026 table reports $16,431,992.54 in county abatements and $10,708,657.83 in hospital district abatements on the combined Winner accounts, excluding tax year 2025. Those amounts sit on the original agreement row, with later rows marked as combined. The report does not isolate an actual credit for order 130032.

sections.heading: What are the Texas data center sales tax exemption requirements?

rows: §151.359 · Qualifying data center
At least 100,000 sq ft in a single building or portion, 20 qualifying jobs, and at least $200 million of eligible investment over five years from certification.
Eligible purchases are exempt from state sales and use tax. Applicable local sales and use tax still applies.
§151.3595 · Qualifying large data center project

At least 250,000 sq ft on a single or eligible contiguous parcel group, 40 qualifying jobs, and at least $500 million of eligible investment over five years. The applicant must agree to contract for at least 20 MW of transmission capacity.
Form 01-929 specifies state and local tax exemption for this section. The statute starts the investment period at the earlier of application or certification.

blocks.text: Both pathways require a qualifying single occupant and facility and purchaser registrations. Eligible costs can include servers, electrical and cooling systems, and qualifying electricity. Review the statutory exclusions for general office or maintenance supplies, certain property incorporated into real estate, and short-term rentals. Source each invoice and determine who claims it.

Check the section on the certificate when reconciling the state guidance. The Comptroller’s web overview repeats state-only wording under the large-project heading and describes the investment period from certification. Form 01-929 distinguishes the two sections’ tax scope, and §151.3595(d)(2)(B) sets the earlier-of clock for large projects. Get the applicable treatment confirmed for the project before including the exemption in a budget.

sections.heading: How do I model the incentive for a site or loan?

blocks.text: Set up annual property tax lines by taxing unit and asset class. Start with the applicable taxable base, then apply the verified contract terms for each tax year. Use the assessor or collector record to corroborate any realized benefit. Put purchases and utility charges on a separate schedule and link each exemption to its certification and invoices.

Use Invariant Earth’s parcel identifier, boundary, and source fields to check which tract you are reviewing. Join the agreement’s legal description and tax accounts against the appraisal district records before applying the terms to the parcel or facility. Examine extensions, remedies and assignment language with the documents for the current transaction.

faqs.answer: Start with the Comptroller’s local development agreement search and the city or county contract archive. Obtain the signed agreement, all amendments, the legal description, and the relevant tax accounts before estimating the benefit.

faqs.question: Does a city property tax abatement make equipment purchases exempt from Texas sales tax?
faqs.answer: Texas sales tax treatment requires the applicable Comptroller facility and purchaser registrations and Form 01-929. Verify the eligible property and statutory section for the purchase separately from the city’s agreement.

faqs.question: How do I verify whether an abatement was actually received?
faqs.answer: Get appraisal or collector records for the relevant account and tax year, and compare them with compliance records or reported amounts. A combined disclosure such as Tarrant County’s Winner LLC row cannot give an actual amount for one expansion by itself.

title: How to Track Proposed Data Center Projects Before Construction
description: Find early project leads in public agendas, approvals and permits. Compare four Loudoun developments and download eight verified application milestones.
coverAlt: Four Loudoun developments with different application outcomes. Golden Substation was approved with conditions, Quantum Park’s amendment was denied, Dulles North had two separate outcomes, and Dulles Technology Park was forwarded for later action.
coverCaption: Selected Loudoun County Board actions from October 20 through November 12, 2026. Each outcome applies to the specific application in the record.
intro: To find proposed data center or industrial projects before construction, start with local planning applications, hearing agendas, and staff reports. Then use the action report, recorded vote, or issued permit to confirm what moved forward. In Loudoun County, Golden Substation went from a scheduling motion in October to approval with conditions in November. description: Download ERCOT historical hub prices and compare day-ahead and real-time settlement intervals. Reproduce the 25-hour Houston and West hub example.
coverAlt: Day-ahead and real-time electricity price lines for the Houston and West trading hubs on November 2, 2025. The two 02:00 intervals appear side by side in a shaded band.
coverCaption: ERCOT’s Houston and West hub settlement prices across the November 2, 2025 operating day. Real-time points are hourly means of four 15-minute prices.
intro: Download the Electric Reliability Council of Texas’s historical hub and load zone workbooks to compare day-ahead and real-time settlement prices. Keep the repeated-hour flag in your join. On November 2, 2025, the Houston hub had two periods labeled 02:00. Their day-ahead prices were $45.35 and $46.86 per MWh, and their real-time hourly means were $42.62 and $30.07. Weight real-time prices by energy used in each interval when modeling a changing load. A simple hourly average is appropriate for a load that stays constant within that hour.

title: County Manufacturing Employment Data from BLS QCEW
description: Download county manufacturing jobs and establishment counts. Compare three Detroit-area counties, reproduce their location quotients and handle suppressed values.
coverAlt: Historic aerial photograph of Ford’s River Rouge industrial complex, the Rouge River and surrounding rail yards.
coverCaption: Ford’s River Rouge complex, circa 1927. Detroit Publishing Company collection, Library of Congress.
intro: For county manufacturing employment, start with the Bureau of Labor Statistics’ Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages. It gives you worksite jobs, establishment counts and industry concentration. In March 2026, Wayne County, Michigan, had 45,124 private transportation equipment manufacturing jobs, the most among the three counties we checked. Macomb County had fewer jobs at 31,414 and the strongest concentration at 8.52 times the national share. Use Invariant Earth to bring broader county employment and physical site evidence into the same shortlist.
takeaways: Compare employment, establishment counts and industry concentration together. They tell you how large the cluster is, how many operating locations it contains and how specialized the local economy is.
Use the same industry code, ownership class and reference month across counties and years. Check the code definition when crossing a classification change.
Preserve suppressed employment values as missing. In early 2026, Macomb County had five published motor vehicle manufacturing establishments and a suppressed job count.

sections.heading: Where can I download manufacturing jobs by county?

blocks.text: Download a county-area CSV from BLS Open Data Access and use the area code, quarter and industry code as part of the record key. For the figures below, we took quarter one of 2024, 2025 and 2026 and used the third month’s employment, the quarter’s establishment count and the third month’s employment location quotient. Select NAICS 31–33 for manufacturing, 336 for transportation equipment manufacturing or 3361 for motor vehicle manufacturing. Our industry rows use private ownership and all establishment sizes.

QCEW employment counts covered jobs at the workplace in the pay period that includes the 12th of the month. Establishments generally correspond to operating locations, and one firm can have several. For a hiring plan, add occupation data, wages and the drive-time labor shed around the candidate site.

sections.heading: Which Detroit-area county has the strongest manufacturing cluster?

blocks.text: We compared Macomb, Oakland and Wayne on the same NAICS 336 definition. Wayne led in total jobs in March 2026. Macomb had the highest location quotient. Oakland’s establishment count rose from 218 to 241 between the first quarters of 2024 and 2026 while March jobs fell from 22,514 to 20,729. Track both measures when deciding whether to investigate plant expansions, hiring or the depth of the local supplier base.

rows: Macomb
Oakland
Wayne

blocks.text: A location quotient divides the industry’s share of all county jobs by its share of all U.S. jobs. BLS uses all industries and ownership classes for both totals. The March 2026 U.S. share for private transportation equipment manufacturing was about 1.12%, based on 1,736,688 industry jobs and 154,771,941 total jobs. A quotient of 8.52 means the industry represented 8.52 times the national share in Macomb.

sections.heading: How should I handle suppressed manufacturing employment?

blocks.text: The narrower motor vehicle manufacturing code changes the picture. Wayne had 29 establishments and 24,244 jobs under NAICS 3361 in the first quarter of 2026. Oakland had 17 establishments and 853 jobs. Macomb published five establishments and withheld employment. We kept the latter value as null. Check both employment and location quotient disclosure fields before reading numeric placeholders, and remember that the broader NAICS 336 total already includes 3361.

When you need a continuous series, look for a broader industry or geography that BLS discloses across the full comparison period. Make that scope visible in the results. For a multi-year comparison, also confirm the industry definition and source vintage. BLS revises its quarterly releases, and changes in reporting geography or industry can move employment between categories.

sections.heading: How do I turn these counts into a manufacturing shortlist?

blocks.text: Use job counts to size the existing cluster and location quotients to find specializations you might miss by sorting on job volume. Economic developers can compare the profiles with peer markets. Manufacturers can use them to pick areas for labor, supplier and freight diligence. Industrial investors can pair multi-year employment and establishment trends with project announcements, lease evidence and proposed construction before underwriting demand.

Invariant Earth’s public field catalog includes countywide annual employment and year-over-year change, parcel IDs and distance to a mapped mainline rail corridor. Pair those fields with the detailed BLS extracts when moving from a county screen to named tracts. For each finalist, verify the usable land, serving railroad and utility commitments against what the facility needs and when it needs it.

title: Historical Hourly Weather Data for Data Center Cooling
description: Compare NOAA hourly temperature and dew point before modeling data center cooling. Reproduce the Phoenix and Dulles results for 2023 to 2025.
coverAlt: A Landsat mosaic of the Phoenix metropolitan area showing its street grid, irrigated green fields and surrounding desert.
coverCaption: Phoenix metropolitan area from Landsat 9 imagery acquired July 3 and July 10, 2024. U.S. Geological Survey.
intro: Use Invariant Earth to compare the climate fields on a site shortlist. Use NOAA’s historical hourly station observations to see how heat and humidity varied before modeling a cooling system. In 2024, Phoenix Sky Harbor recorded 2,149 sampled hours at or above 95°F, compared with 86 at Washington Dulles. Dulles had 981 sampled hours with a dew point at or above 68°F, compared with 67 at Phoenix. The comparison uses outdoor weather at two airports and keeps missing hours visible.
takeaways: Measure dry-bulb temperature and dew point together. Dry-bulb temperature describes the air temperature. Dew point describes its moisture content.
Keep time zone, station ID, report type, quality flags and the number of paired hours. A tally of reports can count the same hour more than once.
Use site-specific design weather, equipment performance and water constraints to evaluate cooling options. The example thresholds here are for comparison.

sections.heading: Where can I download historical hourly temperature and humidity?

blocks.text: Use NOAA NCEI’s GHCNh station files for observed temperature and dew point. NCEI publishes station-year pipe-delimited files and lists Parquet downloads. GHCNh replaces the older Integrated Surface Dataset. Use NOAA’s U.S. Climate Normals when you need a long-term reference instead of observations from particular hours.

Choose a station that represents the site’s elevation and exposure. Keep the observation time in UTC until you intentionally convert to local time. This comparison counts each UTC calendar year and uses airport observations as regional screening examples.

sections.heading: What did the two stations record from 2023 to 2025?

blocks.text: We kept the last eligible routine aviation report in each UTC hour, requiring both dry-bulb temperature and dew point in the same record. We used NOAA’s documented passing quality codes and left unpaired hours missing. We counted 95°F air temperature and 68°F dew point separately and together. These round numbers make the two sites easy to compare.

blocks.text: Phoenix had 145 UTC hours without an eligible pair in 2025, and Dulles had 153. The separate heat and moisture comparisons that year hold even if every missing hour at the station with the lower count reached the corresponding threshold. The small counts for both conditions are more sensitive to missing observations.

sections.heading: How do climate normals and outdoor observations fit into cooling design?

blocks.text: The 1991–2020 normal for the average July daily high is 106.5°F at Phoenix Sky Harbor and 87.6°F at Dulles. Use those values for a long-term baseline. An hourly series answers how often operating conditions co-occur, and the equipment model estimates what the plant consumes at those conditions.

For a design comparison, evaluate coincident dry-bulb and wet-bulb conditions, peak design weather, cooling equipment limits, and the expected IT load. Test water availability, backup operating modes and each design’s part-load behavior. Use outdoor station observations as weather inputs and apply the equipment’s own air and fluid requirements at the relevant operating points.

For an Invariant Earth screening workflow, start with the annual dry-bulb normal, the catalog’s wet-bulb design proxy and the count of hours at or below 15°C in a typical meteorological year. Use the last two as screening inputs with their source and method. Apply coincident hourly conditions and the project team’s design criteria before selecting equipment.

intro: Use the Freight Analysis Framework to compare estimated U.S. freight tonnage and value by origin, destination, mode and commodity. For the current FAF6 benchmark, start with the 2022 state or regional download. We used the state data to trace Canadian motorized vehicles and parts. An estimated 6.06 million tons entered the U.S. through Michigan, while about 3.67 million tons reached destinations in Michigan across all U.S. entry states.
takeaways: For imports, the domestic origin field means where the cargo enters the U.S. The domestic destination is where that U.S. movement ends.

sections.heading: Where do I download U.S. freight flows?

Start with the state data for a statewide corridor comparison. Use FAF regions when a metro-area estimate matters. The 2022 state file reports thousands of tons and millions of 2022 dollars.

Keep the foreign mode and the domestic mode as separate columns. Imported freight can cross into the U.S. on one mode and continue on another. Treat rows in the Multiple Modes and Mail category as their own group. The category can include several kinds of transfers, so use a separate source to estimate the share using a specific terminal.

description: Use OpenFEMA’s current NFIP claims API. Compare Hurricane Ida records and net flood payments in two counties and download the reproducible totals.
coverAlt: Hurricane Ida’s clouds and eye seen from the International Space Station, with the station’s robotic arm in the foreground.
coverCaption: Hurricane Ida seen from the International Space Station. Photograph from NASA.
intro: Use Invariant Earth to check the FEMA flood map at a U.S. site, then use OpenFEMA’s NFIP Redacted Claims v3 to study payment history at county scale. In FEMA’s November 2026 extract, rows tagged to Hurricane Ida in the period we checked sum to about $290.6 million in net building payments in St. John the Baptist Parish, Louisiana, and $63.8 million in Bergen County, New Jersey. The totals describe payments in the federal insurance program and the same storm has a different event code in each state.
takeaways: Use the current endpoint, /api/open/v3/NfipClaims. We tested it on November 23, 2026 and received a valid response. The old FimaNfipClaims v2 endpoint returned 404.
For event analysis, use the loss date, reported county code and storm designation together. Keep rows with blank event tags in a separate count.
Keep building, contents and Increased Cost of Compliance payments in separate fields. Retain the data vintage and use the published county field for geography.

sections.heading: Where do I get FEMA flood insurance claims data?

blocks.text: The live endpoint is https://www.fema.gov/api/open/v3/NfipClaims. Start with countyCode, dateOfLoss, floodEvent, eventDesignationNumber and netBuildingPaymentAmount. Request asOfDate with the data. The OpenFEMA catalog reports the refresh date separately and describes a monthly publication with a lag behind the system of record.

For reproducible totals, filter by the Census county FIPS code and use an inclusive start and exclusive end date. Request a total count with $inlinecount, sort by id and fetch the remaining pages. Check for duplicate record IDs and confirm that the page counts match FEMA’s reported total in a consistent extract.

sections.heading: What did NFIP pay after Hurricane Ida in two counties?

blocks.text: The National Hurricane Center documents Ida’s Louisiana landfall and later flooding in New Jersey. We selected loss dates from August 28 through September 4, 2021, and counted rows tagged Hurricane Ida within that window. All matching rows in these samples show an asOfDate of November 16, 2026. Amounts in the table are net payments after recovery, rounded to the nearest thousand dollars.

rows: St. John the Baptist Parish, Louisiana
Bergen County, New Jersey

blocks.text: A date-only filter returned nine more rows in the Louisiana parish and twenty more in Bergen County. Those rows carried blank event labels in this extract. The benchmark preserves their contribution to the window total separately. There were 3,227 and 1,515 Ida-tagged rows with a positive net building payment, respectively. Use that count when your question is how many records show a positive building payment.

sections.heading: How should a risk team interpret those totals?

blocks.text: The NFIP series reflects losses reported to the federal program. The amount paid depends on the properties that were insured, claims made, and coverage and payment terms. A county payment total answers a different question from economic damage or the number of buildings that flooded. To compare areas across years, carry the reporting vintage, insurance participation and the geography along with the result.

For county reporting, use countyCode rather than assigning records geographically from rounded coordinates. FEMA intentionally reduces coordinate precision for privacy. Use the appropriate flood map edition or modeled hazard evidence to assess the footprint of a particular building. Invariant Earth publishes point-level FEMA fields with their source and vintage. The map and claims aggregate belong in separate measures.

title: Building Footprint Data APIs and Open Datasets
description: Compare Invariant Earth, LightBox, Overture Maps and Microsoft. Test building footprints by address with a Brooklyn Navy Yard mismatch and three NYC polygons.
coverAlt: 2024 overhead photograph of industrial buildings along Flushing Avenue at the Brooklyn Navy Yard.
coverCaption: Brooklyn Navy Yard along Flushing Avenue. Aerial imagery from NYS ITS Geospatial Services, 2024.
intro: Use Invariant Earth when you need building footprint area in the same U.S. coordinate lookup as parcel boundaries, zoning and site hazards. For raw polygons, trial LightBox or download Overture Maps or Microsoft geometry. At Brooklyn Navy Yard, 63 Flushing Avenue is the operator’s address for Building 92. The city geocoder puts that address inside the polygon labeled 280. A lookup for the number 92 returns a different outline on the same tax lot.
takeaways: To get a footprint from an address, resolve the location, retrieve candidate polygons and confirm which structure the customer means. A campus street address can belong to several buildings.
Use a projected coordinate system to measure footprint area. Keep that area separate from gross floor area, insurable square footage and the measurements used for a replacement-cost estimate.
Run the same tests across the counties, building types and historical dates you actually need. Save the returned geometry, source and match decision so another person can reproduce it.

sections.heading: Which source should you start with?

blocks.text: Try primary_building_footprint_sqm and parcel_boundary_geojson together in Earth. The first measures the matched building outline and the second returns the land boundary. Request within_floodplain_polygon in the same lookup to see the FEMA result at the input coordinate. For a building-wide flood screen, intersect the verified building polygon with the flood layer.

Start with how your team will use the data. A live U.S. address workflow needs identifiers and a way to resolve ambiguous results. A regional GIS model needs bulk geometry, a dated release and clear reuse terms. This comparison uses public provider documentation. The Brooklyn test below uses city records independently.

rows: Invariant Earth
Combine Overture-derived footprint area and building characteristics with parcel geometry and other site fields. Each field includes its source.
Check the input coordinate and confirm the matched structure. The documented footprint-area field uses the containing building or the nearest one within 100 metres.
LightBox Structures API
U.S. building lookup by structure ID, parcel or geometry. Related addresses use linked LightBox identifiers.
Can you get all structures on a shared lot and identify which one matches the submission?
Overture Maps Buildings
Bulk GeoParquet for large areas. Parent buildings and building parts are published separately.
Can you track the same structure across releases and keep parts out of the building count? Check source attribution and ODbL terms.
Microsoft Global ML Building Footprints
Download imagery-derived outlines by region and grid tile when you can host and query the data yourself.
Review omissions, merged roofs and new development against imagery from a known date. Plan your own address and parcel join.
Local city or county GIS
Check government-issued identifiers, footprint attributes and linked local records where the authority publishes them.
Check the update date, placeholder geometries and how the source handles a building that spans multiple lots.

sections.heading: A street address can land inside the wrong footprint

blocks.text: We searched NYC GeoSearch for 141 and 63 Flushing Avenue in Brooklyn using the city’s Property Address Directory release 26c. We took each result with the requested house number, street and borough, then used its Building Identification Number (BIN) to query NYC Building Footprints. Both address points landed inside the footprint returned for their BIN. Both footprints carried the same base tax lot number, 3020230001.

For an insurance submission or appraisal at 63 Flushing Avenue, preserve both candidate IDs, compare the outlines with the operator map or a current plan and keep the match open until you can verify the intended building. The city describes its footprint name field as unmaintained, which makes the name match evidence to review.

sections.heading: How do you measure the area of a building footprint?

blocks.text: Measure the polygon in a local projected coordinate system with known units. We requested the NYC geometry in New York Long Island State Plane (EPSG:2263), then measured the enclosed area in square US survey feet. The outline for Building 77 measured about 61,676 square feet. NYC’s metadata advises against using the published Shape_Area value for this purpose.

A footprint measures horizontal extent. A multistory building can have much more floor area than its footprint, and a roof traced in an aerial image can overhang the walls. For lending, use the appraisal or building plan to check the area used for underwriting. For insurance, establish the insured building and get the construction details and dimensions that the replacement-cost method requires.

sections.heading: What should a provider prove in a trial?

blocks.text: Give every provider the same address list, parcels, building labels and known outcomes. Include a campus, a condo with a billing lot, a site with multiple sheds, and a property with a recorded demolition or addition. Ask for the original IDs, the polygons and the data vintage. Look at whether the system forwards uncertain matches for review and whether it can reproduce a result from the quote or credit date.

Score correct building matches, false matches and unresolved cases separately. Evaluate geometry only after verifying the structure. Compare candidate polygons against a trusted reference in the same projection. For a flood or zoning overlay, retain the exact footprint and map edition used so you can tell why the result changed after a new release.

faqs.answer: A footprint outlines a structure viewed from above. A tax parcel describes land for assessment and administration. Brooklyn Navy Yard’s lot 3020230001 had 93 records coded as Building in the NYC footprint layer for this check.

faqs.answer: Calculate the horizontal footprint area in a suitable projected coordinate system. Obtain gross floor area from building plans, an appraisal or an authoritative property record. A footprint leaves the number, size and use of floors open.

Test your provider on the authorities, years and property types in your portfolio before paying for a national feed.

A portfolio monitoring team needs a way to search across markets and catch new records. A lender or underwriter reviewing one building needs the issuer’s record, the work scope and the status as of the credit or quote date. Use the table to choose what to trial. description: Compare Zoneomics, Gridics, Regrid and city GIS APIs. Use a Staten Island tax lot with five mapped zoning districts to test a vendor’s parcel lookup.

coverCaption: 2239 Forest Avenue, Staten Island. The white line traces the MapPLUTO tax lot. Colors show the clipped NYC zoning polygons. Aerial imagery from USDA, USGS and The National Map.
intro: Use Invariant Earth to screen a U.S. location with a cited parcel ID, zoning code, parcel boundary and other site conditions in one lookup. Use city district geometry to measure zoning across a tract. For a U.S. parcel zoning lookup, compare Zoneomics for point and area queries, Gridics for development standards in supported jurisdictions, and Regrid for zoning fields attached to parcel records. Keep the local government’s map and ordinance as your reference. At one Staten Island address, a point lookup gives one district, the city’s tax lot record lists three, and a boundary overlay finds five.
takeaways: Decide whether you need zoning at a coordinate, a parcel summary, or each district intersecting the site.
Ask how the API handles small overlaps and where its source shows the adopted map and rule.
Verify the zoning lot, applicable rules and approvals with the local authority before committing to a use or floor area.

sections.heading: Which zoning API fits the work?

blocks.text: Give every provider the same parcel boundary and proposed use. The commercial comparison below uses published documentation. The five-district result comes from the city data queried for this article.

columns: What to check in a trial
rows: Zoneomics
Point and area lookups, with published options for use tables, controls and overlay data where available.
Submit the parcel polygon and ask for the geometry, source date and permitted-use reference for the affected portion.
Gridics
Parcel-level zoning, uses, setbacks and modeled development capacity.
Check jurisdiction coverage and ask which source rules and parcel assumptions drive a building envelope or floor-area result.
Regrid
Parcel IDs with local zoning codes, standardized categories on applicable plans and a matched zoning product.
Ask when you receive one parcel code, how the code is assigned and which product supplies more detail or a link to the city code.
Invariant Earth
A coordinate lookup returns parcel identity and a Regrid-sourced zoning code alongside other location fields.
Review the matched assessor parcel number. The published catalog allows a nearest-parcel fallback for parcel matching. Use the city district geometry to test the whole tract.
Municipal GIS and code
Local tax maps, district polygons, overlays and the adopted map and ordinance. Format and update process depend on the jurisdiction.
Confirm map and ordinance dates independently. Ask the authority which zoning lot and approvals apply to your plan.

sections.heading: One Staten Island parcel, three different lookup results

blocks.text: We used the MapPLUTO 26v2 boundary for 2239 Forest Avenue, Staten Island, borough-block-lot 5012500011. We also queried NYC Planning’s base zoning district polygons on November 23, 2026. The published parcel point falls in C8-1. MapPLUTO lists M1-1, C4-1 and C8-1 in that order and flags the parcel as split.

The polygon overlay finds five intersections. C4-1 and M1-1 each cover a little over 37% of the mapped tax lot. R3A and R3-2 together cover 7.17%. Both individual shares fall below the 10% minimum defined for MapPLUTO’s base district fields. The two largest districts switch order between the parcel fields and this overlay. The largest areas differ by only 0.35 percentage points in our calculation. Keep the original parcel fields and recomputed results with their own source dates.

title: EV charging station APIs for location and live availability
description: Compare AFDC, TomTom, HERE, Google Places and OCPI. Use two Ohio fast-charging stops to test port counts, connector compatibility and live status.
coverAlt: Aerial map of the I-70 and U.S. Route 42 interchange near London, Ohio, with Pilot 454 and TA London marked.
coverCaption: I-70 Exit 79 near London, Ohio. Pins use AFDC station coordinates. Aerial imagery from USGS, USDA and The National Map.
intro: Use Invariant Earth for site screening around a proposed charger location. One coordinate lookup can bring together parcel, road and utility context. Use charger feeds to plan trips and check connector availability. Use the U.S. Department of Energy’s AFDC API to locate charging stations and count installed ports. For a driver who needs a free connector now, use a timestamped availability feed from a mapping provider or charging network. The difference shows up at one Ohio interchange. The federal inventory lists 16 fast-charging ports across two stops. A routine sum of the equipment export returns 160 because it repeats the station total on each row.
takeaways: Count installed ports once per station ID. Preserve repeated equipment rows when the source supplies no equipment ID.
Keep connector compatibility, station access hours and live equipment status in separate fields.
Ask when the network observed the status. A station record can be updated today and still carry no occupancy data.

sections.heading: Which EV charging API should you use?

blocks.text: Start with the decision you need to support. A planner can use an inventory to find gaps in a corridor. A routing app needs to know whether a compatible charger is free and how recently that was observed. The commercial comparisons below use provider documentation. We queried the AFDC feeds for the Ohio example.

rows: Invariant Earth
Screen a proposed charging location with parcel, road access and electric service territory context.
Check parcel match type and road class. Ask the serving utility to confirm the connection point and capacity for your charging load.
U.S. DOE AFDC
U.S. station inventory with public access, location, connector types and installed DC fast port counts. An equipment CSV adds connector counts and rated power.
Check how station counts repeat across equipment rows and whether the station ID survives a refresh.
TomTom
Charging availability grouped by connector type and power. TomTom documents a three-minute refresh for dynamic data.
Check that both networks appear on your corridor. Measure the age of the underlying status and ask how the feed represents unknown availability.
HERE
Place search with optional connector availability, grouped by type and power. The documentation also covers equipment-level status and operator IDs.
Ask which networks expose equipment detail and usable update timestamps on your routes.
Google Places
Place records with EV connector counts and, where available, compatible-group availability, out-of-service counts and an update time.
Check how often the availability fields populate for the places you serve. Google documents how several connectors can share one charger.
Operator feed via OCPI
Operator-provided Locations, EVSEs and Connectors. The OCPI Locations module defines EVSE status and update fields.
Confirm partner access and keep the country, party, location and equipment IDs needed to match updates.

sections.heading: Two Ohio charging stops expose a 10× counting error

blocks.text: We queried AFDC for electric stations in ZIP 43140 and kept the two public locations with DC fast charging. Both sit at I-70 Exit 79. The equipment export below was captured on November 23, 2026 at 07:31 UTC. It reports equipment inventory and rated output.

rows: Pilot Travel Center 454 · 322368
Four identical rows, each listing one CCS connector rated at 350 kW. Each repeats the station count of 4.
Seven rows list one CCS connector and five list one J3400 connector. All list a 400 kW rating and repeat the station count of 12.

blocks.text: Summing the station field over the equipment rows gives 4 × 4 + 12 × 12 = 160. Counting one station total per AFDC ID gives 4 + 12 = 16. Dropping duplicate-looking CSV rows would also lose equipment detail. The four Pilot rows are identical in the export. AFDC allows an equipment row to describe more than one port or connector, so keep the three quantities separate in your data model.

The Pilot stop also shows why the kW field needs its own label. Ohio’s opening announcement gave a maximum of 350 kW for a single vehicle, with up to 175 kW per port during simultaneous use. Keep the equipment rating for compatibility filters and use a separately sourced power curve or measured data for charging-time estimates.

blocks.label: Download the Ohio station records and port-count audit

sections.heading: Test the answer a driver will see

blocks.text: Suppose a driver with a J3400 inlet wants to stop at TA London. The AFDC export identifies five J3400 connectors there. The station has status E and reports 24-hour public access. That is enough to show a candidate stop. To say how many compatible chargers are free, match the station to a live feed, read the status for the compatible equipment, and retain its update time.

rows: A recent observation with compatible equipment free
Show the count, when it was observed and which connector type it covers.
A recent observation with zero free
Show that no compatible chargers are free. Distinguish ones in use from ones out of service when the feed does.
An old observation
Show when the status was last checked and offer another stop. Set the cutoff using observed delay on that network.
No status, an unknown value, or an unmatched station
Show that live status is unavailable. Keep the inventory and access hours visible.

blocks.text: For the trial, run these two station IDs and add locations from every network you expect customers to use. Compare the API with the operator’s view at the same times over a week. Log whether each station matched, whether it had a timestamp, and how old the observation was when your app received it. Include a known outage and a station with several connectors sharing one charger. Those cases reveal whether the feed can support a routing decision.

title: Geoforge alternatives for data center power screening
description: Compare Geoforge, Paces, PVcase, GridCARE and Invariant. Use 49 PJM upgrade records to test the dates and assumptions behind a data center power forecast.
coverAlt: Illustrative aerial view of transmission towers and a construction lane crossing harvested fields.
coverCaption: AI-generated illustration of a transmission corridor in agricultural terrain.
intro: Start with Invariant for a power study tied to the proposed campus, its load ramp and the dates each phase needs service. Compare Geoforge for candidate connections and modeled offtake, Paces for portfolio screening, PVcase Prospect for grid constraints and GridCARE for utility programs that evaluate flexible load. Give each provider the same test. Ask which facility limits service, when the relevant upgrade enters service and how a delay changes the first phase.
takeaways: In one PJM plan, the same 765 kV line segment had a June 2030 required date and an October 2031 projected date, a gap of 517 days.
AEP Ohio used separate service estimates for different groups of studied customers. One group needed an additional regional upgrade.
A usable power forecast names the connection, the case year, the limiting element and the work required for each load phase.

sections.heading: Which Geoforge alternative fits your site search?

blocks.text: The table summarizes public product descriptions. Use the Ohio example below to test what a provider can explain about its output for your location.

columns: What to ask in the demo
rows: Geoforge
Site reports with potential connections, modeled offtake by year and scenario, queue context and an energization estimate. It also offers deeper power-flow studies.
Ask which grid case and upgrade records drive the range for the first phase. Request the basis for any competing load in that case.
Paces
Regional capacity screening, project-level connection evaluation and support through interconnection studies.
Ask how capacity layer results carry into a study of your site, and which grid, land or permitting issue changes the shortlist.
PVcase Prospect
Modeled injection and withdrawal, with limiting elements for different scenarios. The published documentation distinguishes base-case and contingency coverage by market.
Check the available scenarios for your region and whether the constraint is already present before your load is added.
GridCARE
Utility work on grid capacity for flexible loads. National Grid describes its use in New York and work with UK Electricity Transmission.
Confirm the serving utility is involved and get the MW, hours, operating limits and dispatch conditions for any flexible service.
Invariant
The published site-study workflow covers AC power flow, contingency analysis, candidate connections, and indicative costs and timing.
Request the case vintage, phased results and limiting facilities. Ask which assumptions can be rerun as utility evidence changes.

sections.heading: An Ohio power forecast can contain several valid dates

blocks.text: AEP Ohio’s November 2025 study letter covered about 13 GW of new data center load. It found that the studied projects needed regional transmission work under the scenarios evaluated. Its initial estimate was Q4 2031 for Clusters 1 and 3 with the regional project and applicable parallel upgrades in service. Cluster 2 had a 2033 planning estimate and needed another regional solution. A buyer needs the customer’s actual service plan to determine which work applies.

PJM cross-references the first regional proposal, 2025W1-570, to upgrade package b4068. In the March 2026 assessment, b4068.2, the AEP portion of the Greentown to Teddy 765 kV line, had a required date of June 1, 2030 and a projected date of October 31, 2031. The first is the planning need date. The second is the forecast in that report. A particular customer’s electric service date has its own evidence.

rows: Planning need for b4068.2
June 1, 2030
Keep it as the date the reliability plan requires the work.
Projected in-service date for b4068.2
October 31, 2031
Use it as a dated component forecast and check the latest schedule.
AEP Ohio Cluster 2 service planning estimate
Check the second regional dependency, local work and actual customer schedule.

blocks.text: AEP Ohio later reported that 5,642 MW had signed binding contracts under the new tariff as of February 12, 2026. That update gives the scale of the committed cohort. It leaves the distribution by bus, year and cluster open. Ask your provider how it treats unconfirmed demand, then test a scenario with a different set of competing projects.

sections.heading: What the 49 PJM upgrade rows show

blocks.text: We extracted the required and projected dates for each b4068 sub-ID in the March assessment. Two rows projected June 2028, 21 projected October 2030, and 26 projected October 2031. These are counts of published sub-IDs. A project forecast should identify the subset the connection actually depends on.

Two rows in that assessment show an invalid calendar value in the required-date column. The February board recommendations show June 1, 2030 for both sub-IDs. The download retains the February dates and the March source values separately, with the latter normalized to null. Ask a provider which source its model used and how it handles this sort of discrepancy.

sections.heading: How to test the first phase before paying for a site option

blocks.text: Give the vendor the parcel, the minimum load needed on day one, the full facility load, the two service dates and how much load you can curtail. For example, ask for 50 MW by July 2030 and 200 MW by January 2032 at the meter. Those are illustrative targets, with the utility service for your project to be confirmed.

items: Ask for the modeled MW on each date at the same connection point. Record the model year, the limiting equipment and the outage assumption.
Request a second run with the relevant upgrade out of service through your target date. Ask which phase remains feasible and what changes the answer.
Get the utility’s written service terms, required work and estimated start of service. Keep energization and facility handover as separate milestones.

faqs.answer: Consider Paces for portfolio screening, PVcase Prospect for modeled point-of-interconnection constraints, GridCARE for opportunities that depend on utility-supported load flexibility, and Invariant for a phased site study. Test your actual service dates with each provider.

faqs.question: What is the difference between required and projected in-service dates?
faqs.answer: The required date expresses when the planning case needs an upgrade. The projected date is the schedule estimate in that record. PJM’s March 2026 assessment lists June 1, 2030 and October 31, 2031 respectively for b4068.2. Use the relevant utility agreement and construction schedule to evaluate customer service.

faqs.answer: A power screen can estimate when the grid could support a proposed load under a specific case. The serving utility’s agreement and work plan establish the commercial service terms and estimated date. Confirm energization through a commissioning or utility record.

title: Ageospatial alternatives for commercial roof underwriting
description: Compare Ageospatial, Moody’s, ZestyAI, Verisk and Invariant Earth with a real test for building identity, roof replacement dates and source evidence.
coverAlt: Aerial view of the Rosemead Public Works warehouse with its county building footprint outlined.
coverCaption: 2022 USDA NAIP imagery via CDFW. The outline marks the building identified on the city site map. The photo predates the 2025 roof work.
intro: Use Invariant Earth to start underwriting with a cited building and parcel record, then attach the roof evidence to the structure that the submission covers. Compare Ageospatial for a workflow that collects imagery, maps and records, and Moody’s, ZestyAI and Verisk for dedicated roof products. Give each provider a submission with two addresses and three dates for the same roof project. Check which structure and event the result describes.
takeaways: Compare products on the exact building and roof scope. The owner’s mailing address can point to a different property.
A replacement project has an award date, a completion date and a date when the evidence became available to your team. Keep all three.
A roof age estimate, a report of completed work and a current condition rating answer different underwriting questions.

sections.heading: Which Ageospatial alternative fits your workflow?

blocks.text: Decide what the underwriter needs to do with the answer. An inspection team may need a roof and imagery report. A quoting team may need a structured age field with a confidence signal. A data team may need the building match, its source and a way to store later corrections. The comparison below uses public product descriptions. The municipal records provide an independent case you can run with each vendor.

columns: What to ask for in a trial
rows: Ageospatial
Workflow examples tie a submission line to the parcel and footprint, show a dated roof image, and flag changes and nearby exposures.
Have the tool link each finding to the original record. Export the resolved building, both addresses and the dates behind the replacement finding.
Moody’s Commercial Property Intelligence
Commercial building and roof data, including imagery-derived age and condition, with API, batch and application delivery.
Ask what drove the age estimate for the selected commercial roof and whether the output can show a date range or leave the age open.
ZestyAI Roof Age
Roof replacement estimates from imagery and permit records, with confidence and modeled values where direct evidence is sparse. ZestyAI describes use in a commercial portfolio.
Ask how the model distinguishes a full replacement from partial work and which fields expose the evidence or model basis.
Verisk Roof Underwriting Report
A commercial roof report with age, condition, material, equipment and an estimated roof replacement cost.
Review the target location and scope of the reported age and cost. Ask what can be retained as machine-readable data.
Invariant Earth
A coordinate-based API with fields for the primary building footprint area, height, floor count and class where supported.
Use the field catalog to choose the spatial inputs. Establish the roof event from the city record and retain it alongside the matched building in your workflow.

sections.heading: The Rosemead test starts with two addresses

blocks.text: Rosemead’s July 2025 notice attachment gives 8838 E Valley Boulevard as the city’s address and 2714 River Avenue as the location where the roof work took place. The project documents identify the Public Works Office and Warehouse Building at the River Avenue site. The site map on page TP-1 points to that building among several neighboring roofs.

Even the correct street address can produce different coordinates. The Census Geocoder returned an address-range coordinate that intersects no outline in the county’s 2023 building layer. The county address point was about 64 meters away, carried assessor parcel ID 5282026900 and intersected county outline 2920695. The outline matches the building shape pointed to on the city’s map. The county address record itself has a blank building ID.

That matters in a coordinate-based API. Invariant Earth describes its primary footprint field as using the enclosing Overture building or searching within 100 meters for the nearest one. Keep the input coordinates and review the returned match against the project map before using the result in the file. The county outline in the aerial cover is shown for identification. The photograph is from 2022.

sections.heading: When did the roof actually change?

rows: January 14, 2025
The city awarded the roof replacement contract.
A named project and planned scope.
June 2, 2025
Completion date stated in the notice attachment in the July packet.
The reported date of the replacement work and the later source document date.
July 8, 2025
The council accepted the work and authorized recording the notice.
The acceptance action and authority to record. The county recording date remains unverified.

blocks.text: The staff report says the old metal roofing system was removed and a new metal system installed. The final project cost included additional cooler work. Store that amount as project expenditure and request a cost breakdown or a separate estimate when you need the replacement cost of the roof alone.

For a hypothetical June 30 quote supported only by the records dated by then, keep the replacement completion field open. At a July 31 review with the July packet in hand, add the reported June 2 completion as a new piece of evidence and keep the prior quote snapshot. A dated inspection would answer a separate question about the roof’s current condition.

title: Mireye Alternatives for U.S. Property Screening
description: Compare Mireye, Invariant Earth, West Kite, and Regrid for U.S. property screening. Check how each handles parcel matches, hazards, and utility evidence.
coverAlt: Illustrative aerial view of an industrial building beside winding wetlands.
coverCaption: AI-generated illustration of an industrial site beside wetlands.
intro: Use Invariant Earth when your workflow needs cited site conditions, parcel boundaries and the reason a parcel was matched. Compare Mireye for public location fields and parcel enrichment, West Kite for lot-level flood and wetland overlap, and Regrid for parcel geometry and identity. Run the same property through each workflow and check which location and source produced each result.
takeaways: Compare the coordinates and geometry behind each field. The same field name can describe a different search or source.
Both Mireye and Invariant use wetland_acres for an entire selected wetland polygon. To estimate affected acreage, calculate its intersection with the property or project area.
Bring the same assessor parcel, hazard map and required service level to each trial. Record the provider’s matching, missing data and source dates.

sections.heading: Which tool should you evaluate?

blocks.text: Invariant makes Invariant Earth. We reviewed public catalogs and documentation on November 22, 2026. The comparison describes documented inputs and outputs. Test account-specific coverage, latency, and results on your own properties.

columns: What to check in a trial
rows: Mireye
Point data through Fetch or parcel records through Enrich.
Compare the input coordinate with Enrich’s analysis_point. Its documented example resolves a parcel and uses the stored parcel centroid for analysis.
Invariant Earth
Location and parcel fields with field-level source, dataset vintage and status.
Inspect parcel_match_type and parcel_match_distance_m. The parcel ID can fall back to a nearest parcel within 250 meters. Check the match before joining another dataset.
West Kite
Commercial property research and a report using the parcel outline for flood and wetland area.
Check the property match and whether each layer is published for the county. The documented response identifies fields that could not be answered.
Regrid
Parcel IDs and boundaries for use in your own GIS or pipeline.
Use the county record to verify a recent split. Regrid explains which events preserve its ID and which retire it.

sections.heading: Four fields to verify before switching

blocks.text: Mireye publishes separate catalogs for Fetch and Enrich. Invariant lists parcel-match fields in its location catalog. Check the catalog for the endpoint that will serve the workflow. The download records the field name, published unit, source identifier, and what to verify for each output.

rows: Is the location in a mapped flood zone?
Both document within_floodplain_polygon as a FEMA Special Flood Hazard Area test at a point.
For land or buildings, intersect the full geometry with the effective FEMA polygons. Keep the map date and area by zone.
How many wetland acres affect the tract?
Both define wetland_acres as the total area of the selected National Wetlands Inventory polygon. It can be the nearest wetland, including one outside the tract.
Intersect mapped wetlands with the tax lot or proposed disturbance area, then calculate the acreage inside it.
Which substation should we investigate?
Both expose nearest_substation_distance_m. Invariant lists a 10 km search. Mireye describes an EIA layer for substations at 69 kV or above.
Save the returned facility, layer and method. Confirm the serving utility and proposed connection before relying on a capacity estimate.
How reliable is the water service map?
Both expose water_service_area_provenance. Invariant describes the boundary method and original provider. Mireye describes source-based and modeled categories.
Save the original evidence. Ask the utility about pressure, flow, and a service commitment for the intended use.

blocks.text: Pick a candidate whose boundary you already know. Submit the assessor’s location point and a second point inside the proposed work area. Keep the site address and county parcel ID fixed. Request the parcel boundary separately and record where each result was evaluated. Include a multi-parcel site in the trial when that is part of your usual work.

Use the same source layer and edition when reconciling values. At Brooklyn Army Terminal, for example, the published location point returned FEMA Zone AE. Intersecting the parcel boundary with the same map showed that about 20% of the lot was in Zone AE. The parcel overlay below includes the source queries so you can repeat the calculation.

Save the field status with the value. Mireye Fetch and Invariant Earth document a distinction between a successful value, no data at a location, and a failed field request. A successful response can include a failed field. Store the dataset edition separately from the fetch time, especially when you are recreating an earlier decision.
