title: How to Check Wildfire Risk by Address for Commercial Property
description: Match the right building, verify the wildfire map and its date, and document what needs inspection. Includes two reproducible Los Angeles address checks.
coverAlt: Illustration of a commercial building at the edge of dry Southern California hills.
coverCaption: Illustration of a fictional site. The Los Angeles checks below use public map records.
intro: Start with the building on the submission. Match its address to a footprint, check which wildfire map applies, and save the map result with the source and date. At Griffith Observatory, two county address points for the same facility are about 33 meters apart. The two points return the same hazard category. Only one intersects the mapped building. The location check is useful even when the zone result agrees.
takeaways: Keep the matched building ID and the way the address was located. A street point can return a valid map category for the wrong building.
Keep the published hazard category, map edition and source record. A mapped NonWildland result is different from missing coverage.
Request current evidence for the roof, vents, nearby combustibles and access before evaluating the building’s susceptibility to wildfire.

sections.heading: Match the address to the building on the submission

blocks.text: Use the street address, ZIP code and building or suite identifier to find candidate locations. At a commercial campus, check the building on the statement of values, which lists the locations and amounts submitted for insurance. Confirm the address against an owner-provided site plan or other building record. Keep each building as its own record when several structures share a parcel or mailing address. County address datasets can contain multiple source points and omit some units.

Record whether the location came from a building, parcel, street segment or ZIP code. A point that falls inside a building is stronger evidence than a street estimate. Review the footprint’s source date and compare it with current records for additions, replacements or multiple structures at the same address.

sections.heading: Two Los Angeles buildings on the 2025 CAL FIRE map

blocks.text: We matched the facilities’ published addresses to county address points and building outlines, then queried the complete polygons against the State Fire Marshal’s 2025 recommended layer for Local Responsibility Areas. Both buildings were within a single mapped class. The county outlines report 2008 source imagery with an Unchanged status in the queried service.

rows: Griffith Observatory, 2800 East Observatory Road
County building ID 470757865499. One of two candidate points intersects the outline. The other is about 25 meters from it.
Very High, raw code 3. The complete mapped footprint falls within a single Very High feature.
Los Angeles Central Library, 630 W. 5th Street
County building ID 484322840870. The address point intersects the outline.
NonWildland, raw code −3. The complete mapped footprint falls within that mapped category.

blocks.text: CAL FIRE’s layer returned NonWildland as a record for the library. A service timeout, a query outside map coverage or a point that returned no features should have a different status. The city’s separate Very High zone layer also matched the Observatory footprint and returned no intersection for the library. Confirm the locally applicable map and its effective date with the jurisdiction for any dated decision.

sections.heading: Save the map version and the relationship to the zone

blocks.text: California’s Fire Hazard Severity Zones describe long-term hazard using vegetation, terrain, fire weather and other factors. To find the map for an address, start with the responsibility area. CAL FIRE publishes State Responsibility Area maps, and the State Fire Marshal provides recommended Local Responsibility Area zones. Ask the local jurisdiction which map was in effect on your decision date. Record the publisher, layer, version, effective date where verified, retrieval date and original class.

Compare the full building outline with every intersecting polygon. Keep the classes and whether the building is inside, crosses a boundary, or only touches its edge. Route uncertain matches and mixed footprints for review, especially when a source point or older footprint can change the result. Keep the raw response so the decision can be reviewed after the source updates.

For portfolios outside California, start with the applicable state or local source. The U.S. Forest Service’s Wildfire Risk to Communities data can help prioritize regions to investigate. The Forest Service describes it as a community-scale resource and cautions against using it at the individual-property scale.

sections.heading: What to keep in the underwriting file

blocks.text: Use public mapping to document exposure and direct the next review. The California Department of Insurance describes CAL FIRE’s severity maps as planning tools and explains that insurers use separate wildfire risk models for underwriting and pricing. Keep the map result beside the carrier’s distinct model result and version, where your workflow uses one.

Submitted address, building ID, match method, footprint date and unresolved matches.
Owner’s building schedule or a site plan when a parcel contains more than one structure.
Mapped hazard
Publisher, map version, date, zone label, footprint relation and any coverage gap.
Local map or adoption record for the decision date when required.
Fire history
Perimeter source, data version, time period and relationship to the building.
Inspection, repair or loss records for questions about damage to a specific structure.
Building susceptibility
Roof covering and condition, vents, openings, vegetation, combustible storage and access.
Dated inspection, photographs or maintenance records that identify the building and conditions reviewed.
Insurance decision
Which evidence informed the referral, unresolved questions, and the carrier’s applicable terms or model output.
Carrier guidance and the applicable policy or binder.

blocks.text: A historical perimeter indicates a mapped past event. CAL FIRE describes gaps and generalization in those records, including areas inside a perimeter that may have escaped burning. A building intersection is a reason to check loss or inspection records. For the condition review, IBHS’s commercial guidance identifies components worth examining, including roofs, vents and nearby combustible material.

sections.heading: Which commercial property policies does SB 547 cover?

blocks.text: California Insurance Code section 675.55 applies to eligible commercial property policies already in force at the time of the emergency declaration. The one-year protection concerns cancellation or nonrenewal based solely on the structure’s location in an area where a wildfire occurred. Section 675.1 addresses residential policies.

For ordinary commercial property, the size exclusion requires both an annual premium of at least $25,000 and an average of at least 25 employees in the preceding 12 months. The statute overrides that size exclusion for policies covering loss or damage to real property used primarily for commercial residential or habitational purposes, such as apartment complexes and qualifying association property. Inland marine, transit and transportation policies are separately excluded. Section 675.55(b) sets out additional exceptions.

sections.heading: A renewal in ZIP code 95370

blocks.text: ZIP code 95370 appears in both bulletins. Suppose a commercial property policy for a building there first took effect October 1, 2026. It was in force on the Dove declaration date and began after the Gann declaration date. Bring the Dove bulletin into the review and record the policy inception date alongside both matches. The reviewer still needs the policy type, applicable exclusions and the insurer’s stated reason.

For notices that meet the bulletin’s conditions, the Department directs insurers to offer to rescind wildfire-related cancellation or nonrenewal notices and offer reinstatement or renewal. A policyholder can ask the carrier to review the notice against the applicable bulletin and contact the Department for assistance when needed.

sections.heading: What to save in the underwriting file

items: Save the insured address and ZIP from the policy schedule, with the bulletin number and source page. Keep one record per fire and ZIP so overlapping events remain visible.
Record the declaration date, bulletin issue date, policy effective date, notice date, notice reason and proposed end date.
For commercial property, capture the policy form and principal use, and record the annual premium and average employment when the statutory exclusion requires them.
Route conflicting dates, uncertain address matches and policies covering multiple locations for review with the supporting records.

blocks.text: The Department distinguishes CAL FIRE’s Fire Hazard Severity Zone maps, used for planning, from insurers’ wildfire risk models. The bulletin ZIP list answers a separate question about which areas the agency identified for a specific renewal protection.

title: How to verify a shovel-ready industrial site
description: See what industrial site certification covers and verify buildable land, power, water, wastewater and permits. Compare two certified Tennessee sites.
coverAlt: Two certified Tennessee sites compared against an example requirement of 25 developable acres and 3 million gallons per day of water system headroom.
coverCaption: Published figures for the Canterbury and I-40 Advantage sites against an illustrative screen. Water figures refer to the system’s reported excess capacity.
intro: A shovel-ready designation tells you what a site program reviewed. To decide whether a factory can start on schedule, check the exact tract, the accepted land use, the usable acreage and the utilities that can commit to the project. Two sites in the same Tennessee certification announcement illustrate the difference. One clears the example acreage requirement. The other clears the initial water screen.
takeaways: Keep the certifying program, date and tract boundary with the designation.
Compare usable site area with the latest layout and keep related acreage figures tied to their original boundaries.
Ask each provider for a service offer at the proposed connection point, including the project’s volume, required upgrades and delivery date.
Publish an evidence date and a next action for every open constraint in the inventory.

sections.heading: What shovel-ready certification covers

blocks.text: Select Tennessee’s published criteria call for at least 20 developable acres, truck-quality access, documented site conditions and utilities onsite or a formal extension plan. The program accepts current zoning or an expedited rezoning plan. Those are meaningful signals to start with. For a buyer, the difference between an installed connection and an extension plan can be months of work.

Read the actual program rules when comparing badges. Kentucky’s separate Build-Ready designation builds on its shovel-ready criteria and requires a completed, engineer-certified pad for a building of at least 50,000 square feet, with room to expand to at least 100,000. The building pad and its expansion area are distinct from the gross tract acreage.

The state’s public listings report different combinations of acreage, zoning and utility characteristics. The table uses the public records as reviewed on November 22, 2026. faqs.answer: Check the certifying program and the provider’s evidence. Tennessee’s program can accept a formal extension plan. The provider’s service offer should identify the connection, offered capacity, upgrades and date for your project.

faqs.answer: Shovel-ready describes the work and evidence required by the program. A pad-ready claim concerns a specific building pad. For example, Kentucky’s Build-Ready standards require a completed pad certified by a licensed engineer. Ask for the certification and the pad dimensions.

title: How to check FEMA flood zone history for commercial property underwriting
description: Check which FEMA flood map applied on a quote or loan date. Use building footprints, effective dates and map revision records to audit commercial flood exposure.
coverAlt: Current FEMA map zones within the Huntington revision area, beside a timeline of the July 2021 issue date, December 2021 effective date and January 2024 Alexandria panel.
coverCaption: Current FEMA flood zones inside the Huntington revision boundary. The revision took effect in December 2021 and FEMA later incorporated it into a revised Alexandria panel.
intro: To check a commercial building’s FEMA flood zone on a past date, match the insured building to its footprint, find the map panel effective on that date and apply any map changes that were already in force. Save the map and change records with the decision. An address-only lookup against today’s National Flood Hazard Layer gives you a current result and can miss the history that mattered on the quote date.
takeaways: Record the insured building, map panel and effective date, applicable FEMA case number, and when the result was retrieved.
Track issue dates, effective dates and later panel publication separately. A single FEMA revision can have all three.
Keep mapped flood zones, modeled depth, expected loss and any required lender determination in separate fields.

sections.heading: Match the building before you look up the zone

blocks.text: For Brooklyn Army Terminal tax lot 3057780001, FEMA returned Zone AE at the coordinate published in MapPLUTO. The point was about 9 meters outside the shoreline-clipped tax lot. description: Compare NOAA hail reports and radar estimates at a building. A Denver example shows what a five-kilometer search can tell a commercial underwriter.

intro: To check hail history by address, locate the building on the policy or submission. Then search dated hail reports around it and read the radar grid over the building for the same time window. sections.heading: Two points in the same Denver hailstorm

blocks.text: On May 30, 2024, severe storms crossed metropolitan Denver. We took two illustrative locations 4.15 km apart and searched the same NOAA hail episode from 8 p.m. to midnight Mountain Daylight Time. For each point we kept records with a published start location and a reported hail size within 5 km. Both searches returned the same 2.75-inch report as their largest. The point nearest that report had a radar estimate of 1.42 inches. The other had a radar estimate of 0.55 inches.

sections.heading: Check the time zone and the units

blocks.text: Storm Events records the 2.75-inch report start as May 30 at 21:12 with the offset MST-7. That converts to 10:12 p.m. on May 30 in Denver daylight time and 04:12 UTC on May 31. The matching radar window spans 02:00 to 06:00 UTC on May 31. A search restricted to May 30 UTC would miss the evening storm.

The radar product is NOAA’s Maximum Estimated Size of Hail, or MESH. Its 240-minute file stores each cell’s peak estimate for the preceding four hours in millimeters. Divide by 25.4 to compare those values with reports in inches. Keep the timestamp and window length together so a later reader can reproduce the search.

An earlier file ending at 8 p.m. local time returned the raw code −1 for both cells. NOAA lists −1 as missing and −3 as no coverage. Store the numeric estimate as unknown alongside the original code. In the download, each source file has a URL and checksum. The download uses a later version of the bulk archive. For a point-in-time review, use the file version you actually had on the decision date.

intro: Use Invariant Earth when your underwriting team needs to verify the parcel and inspect the sources behind building and hazard fields. Evaluate Cotality for building prefill and reconstruction cost, Moody’s CAPE for imagery-derived roof attributes, Verisk for commercial underwriting reports, and Guidewire HazardHub for peril and fire-protection data. sections.heading: Which building is on the submission?

blocks.text: A statement of values lists the locations and values submitted for insurance. Consider a line for Building A at Brooklyn Army Terminal, 140 58th Street. The city’s municipal benchmarking report identifies Building A as Building Identification Number (BIN) 3257059 on tax lot 3057780001. The operator’s specification describes eight stories, a height of 89 feet, and approximately 500,000 square feet of floor area. We used those records to check what the building lookup returned.

The exact BIN matched a footprint in NYC’s building dataset on that tax lot. The footprint record reported a roof height of 14 feet and a construction year of 2022. Those values disagree with the operator’s description of Building A. Preserve the returned outline as a candidate, ask for a verified building plan or footprint, and leave building-level exposure pending. This is a useful test even for providers that report a confident address match.

The same campus illustrates what can happen downstream. Our parcel screen found a FEMA Zone AE overlap on 19.9% of the shoreline-clipped lot. Copying that result to a building record would change the scope of the evidence. After resolving the building outline, intersect it with the relevant map edition and keep the map, geometry and date used for the result.

title: Historical parcel boundaries API guide for splits and mergers
description: Trace an old parcel ID through a split or merger. Compare two real NYC tax map changes with dated boundaries, source queries, and a downloadable crosswalk.
coverAlt: Side-by-side boundary maps show Brooklyn block 3947 before and after its November 20 split. Lot 1 shrinks from about 45,290 to 24,121 square feet, and new lot 105 takes about 21,169 square feet.
coverCaption: Brooklyn block 3947. Same scale before and after. Boundaries from MapPLUTO 26v2 and NYC Tax Lot Polygon, checked against tax map alteration 738545. Areas are calculated from mapped geometry.
intro: A historical parcel lookup needs two things. The boundary that applied on the date you care about, and the relation between that parcel and the lots that came before or after it. A current parcel ID can survive even when its footprint changes. In Brooklyn on November 20, 2026, lot 1 on block 3947 kept its ID after a split, with about 53% of its former mapped area. A merger on another block that day retired two IDs and enlarged a third.
takeaways: Store dated geometry separately from the parcel number and keep both versions when the source preserves the same ID.
Use the local alteration record to tell a split from a merger, a map correction, or a new survey.
Validate the match with the old and new geometries, then keep source edition, change date, and observation date in the result.

sections.heading: A split where the old ID stayed in use

blocks.text: On Brooklyn block 3947, NYC’s older tax map shows one lot, numbered 1, at the Atlantic Avenue end of the block. The November 20 map shows lot 1 and lot 105 separated by a new internal boundary. Alteration 738545 labels lot 1 affected and lot 105 new. The borough, block, and lot identifier, known as a BBL in New York City, gives lot 1 the same value of 3039470001 on both versions.

The predecessor footprint measured about 45,290 square feet in the earlier geometry. After the split, the two footprints measured about 24,121 and 21,169 square feet. A query for the old BBL against today’s parcel layer can return lot 1 successfully and still omit almost half of the original footprint. The crosswalk returns both successors for an old record and assigns each boundary its own record ID.

sections.heading: A merger where two IDs disappeared

blocks.text: On Brooklyn block 3373, alteration 739346 marks lots 1 and 2 as dropped and lot 57 as affected. The prior map shows all three at the Broadway end of the block. The later map shows one enlarged lot 57. A lookup for either dropped BBL in the later geometry returned no row, but both historical footprints intersect the enlarged successor. The crosswalk also carries the old version of lot 57 forward to its expanded version.

blocks.text: Query the city’s alteration tables by transaction number for the change date, type, and lot actions. faqs.question: Does a parcel number change after a split?
faqs.answer: It depends on the jurisdiction and the split. In the Brooklyn example, one successor kept the original BBL and another received a new BBL. The older and newer geometries for the retained BBL have distinct footprints.

faqs.question: How can I find the owner of a commercial building by address?
faqs.answer: Find the parcel identifier in the local assessor or GIS system. Then search the recorder using that identifier, inspect the latest applicable conveyances, and compare the parties with the assessor’s owner field. Resolve conflicting results using the original records.

faqs.question: Can an LLC registry reveal who owns the underlying real estate?
faqs.answer: A registry can confirm the company’s identity and public filings. The property deed establishes the grantee for a recorded transfer. To verify the company’s investors or control rights, look for dated agreements, regulatory disclosures or documents from the company.

faqs.question: Why does a property have two deeds on the same day?
faqs.answer: The property may pass through an intermediate party before reaching the final grantee. Keep each deed’s recording identifier and connect the first grantee to the next grantor. In the GM Building example, the two June 9, 2008 deeds record exactly that sequence.

faqs.question: Can control change while the ownership percentage stays the same?
faqs.answer: Yes. In 2013, BXP reported that its 60% economic interest in the GM Building venture stayed the same when the venture’s partners and decision rights changed.

title: Flood Risk APIs for U.S. Properties
description: Compare FEMA flood zone APIs and modeled flood depth for underwriting and site selection. Reproduce four tests using Hurricane Ida high-water marks.
coverAlt: 2024 aerial view of Brooklyn connecting an Ida high-water mark in Gowanus, FEMA Zone AE, and a mark in Prospect Park, FEMA Zone X.
coverCaption: Markers show two USGS survey points after Ida in 2021. Their FEMA zones come from a November 2026 query. Background is 2024 New York State aerial imagery.
intro: Use Invariant Earth when you need a cited point-level FEMA flood screen alongside parcel and building context. Review the FEMA result and its vintage, then check the footprint against the effective map for a building-level decision. For the effective FEMA zone at a U.S. property, start with the National Flood Hazard Layer or an API that returns the original zone, subtype and map panel. For potential flood depth and damage, use a model that specifies the event probability, year and scenario. For evidence that water reached a location during a particular storm, look for surveyed marks or mapped inundation from that event. A property file can benefit from all three.
takeaways: Save the FEMA zone, subtype, Special Flood Hazard Area flag and panel effective date together.
Treat a surveyed high-water mark as evidence about one location and storm. Keep the surveyed water elevation and the height of the mark above ground in separate fields.
Require a vertical datum whenever an API reports elevation. Preserve missing values and confirm why a base flood elevation is missing before using it.

sections.heading: Which flood risk API fits your workflow?

blocks.text: For regulatory mapping, compare the FEMA feature and panel you get back. For underwriting or site selection, get the building match and an estimate of how deep water could get, then review the assumptions. This comparison uses public documentation checked November 23, 2026. The test below uses FEMA and USGS data directly. Invariant publishes the comparison and makes Invariant Earth.

Effective flood hazard polygons, map panels and published base flood elevations where available.

Request depth for the same building under two return periods and save the year, scenario, percentile and depth unit.

Flood fields alongside other commercial property and peril attributes.
Ask which fields come from FEMA. Request the source and method behind any separate risk score.
Mireye
Cited location and parcel screening, including FEMA exposure.
Ask for the geometry used in the result, and test whether a point result changes when the footprint spans a boundary.

Cited point-level FEMA screening, with a published null policy for static base flood elevation.

sections.heading: What Hurricane Ida’s water marks show about FEMA Zones X and AE

blocks.text: On September 1, 2021, remnants of Hurricane Ida brought flash flooding to New York City. USGS later surveyed marks left by the water. At the Third Street Bridge in Gowanus, a mark on stairs near a generator stood 1.63 feet above ground. About 1.1 miles away near the Third Street Playground in Prospect Park, a mark on a lamp post stood 3.23 feet above ground. The two points are on the same NYC Flood Insurance Rate Map panel. The FEMA hazard layer we queried on November 23, 2026 returned Zone AE in Gowanus and unshaded Zone X in Prospect Park.

sections.heading: Keep water depth separate from elevation

blocks.text: Base flood elevation is a mapped water-surface elevation for the 1% annual-chance flood. It uses a named vertical datum, the reference surface for the height. At the Gowanus sample, FEMA’s static value is 10 feet in NGVD29. USGS recorded the observed water-surface elevation as 9.2 feet in NAVD88. Subtracting those figures directly would mix two reference surfaces. Use an appropriate datum transformation before comparing elevations and keep the original values. For first-floor exposure, obtain a floor elevation or certified building information tied to the correct structure.

A Zone A point can have no static base flood elevation even though the point is inside the mapped Special Flood Hazard Area. In this test, FEMA returns the sentinel value −9999 for the Levy Playground point. The download preserves that value and normalizes it to null. A missing static field may also require reading a flood profile or a separate elevation layer.

sections.heading: What to require from a property flood API

items: Match the actual structure. Save the exact point or footprint, address-match method and source vintage. Retain multiple intersections when a building crosses a mapped flood boundary.
Keep the effective panel, zone subtype, and parcel or footprint overlap. Retrieve applicable map changes and follow the required determination process for lending.
Record the flood model’s peril, probability, horizon, scenario and depth reference. Save the source version so a later model update remains visible in the file.
Track storm observations with the event date, survey location and quality. Use a separate field for areas where the provider checked and found no applicable record.

faqs.question: Does FEMA Zone X mean a property cannot flood?
faqs.answer: No. Check the subtype, which may indicate minimal mapped hazard, a moderate hazard area, or another map condition. During Ida, USGS documented flood marks at locations that a later FEMA query classified as unshaded Zone X.

faqs.question: Is base flood elevation a depth above the ground?
faqs.answer: Base flood elevation is a water-surface elevation referenced to a vertical datum. To compare it with ground or floor elevation, use the same datum and units. Some zones report a mapped depth instead, and others have no published static elevation at that point.

faqs.question: Can I use a flood model instead of the FEMA map for a lender determination?
faqs.answer: A flood model can inform underwriting. Use the applicable flood determination process and effective FEMA records for a lender’s regulatory determination. Match the structure and check any applicable map changes.

faqs.question: How do I test a flood risk API before buying it?
faqs.answer: Use points with known FEMA zones, a point with no published static elevation, a building that spans zones, and a dated storm observation. Check the raw source, input geometry, dates, units, datum and treatment of missing values.

title: Commercial Mortgage Maturity Data and APIs
description: Find and verify a commercial mortgage maturity date. Compare CMBS APIs and test how they handle amendments, extension options, and dated source records.
coverAlt: Timeline showing Orion’s original February 2027 maturity, the amended February 2029 maturity, and conditional options in February and August 2030.
coverCaption: Orion Properties disclosed the amendment on February 19, 2026. The two 2030 dates depend on borrowers exercising their options and meeting the agreement’s conditions.
intro: Use Invariant Earth to put parcel, building and flood evidence in a commercial collateral file. Link that file to loan records from your servicer or a loan data provider before tracking maturity. To find when a U.S. commercial mortgage matures, start with the current schedule from your servicer or the trust’s latest loan-level report. Check any amendments and confirm whether the borrower exercised an extension option. A county mortgage index helps identify the instrument, but you may need the actual loan documents to establish the due date. For a portfolio spanning many lenders, ask any data provider exactly which loans it covers and which document supports each date.
takeaways: Keep the original maturity, current stated maturity and conditional option dates in separate fields.
Store the date an amendment took effect, the date its source was published, and the date your system obtained it.
Use a stable loan identifier for the debt and a separate relationship to every property securing it. Count the balance once even when the loan covers multiple properties.

sections.heading: How a $355 million commercial mortgage changed maturity

blocks.text: Orion Properties’ November 2026 Form 10-Q identifies an original $355 million securitized loan. At origination it was scheduled to mature on February 11, 2027. The February 17, 2026 modification moved the stated maturity to February 11, 2029. Orion filed the agreement on February 19. At September 30, Orion reported $316.5 million outstanding on the loan, which was secured by 18 properties.

faqs.question: Where can I find the maturity date of a commercial mortgage?
faqs.answer: Ask the servicer for the current schedule and check it against the note and later amendments. For covered CMBS loans, look up the trust and loan ID in the latest asset-level filing. For public borrowers, Form 10-Q debt footnotes and material agreement exhibits can confirm changes.

faqs.question: What is the difference between stated and extended maturity?
faqs.answer: Stated maturity is the scheduled due date under the operative terms. A signed amendment can move that date. A conditional option gives the borrower a right to move the date further after meeting the conditions. Confirm exercise before using the option date as the current due date.

faqs.question: How often do commercial mortgage maturity dates update?
faqs.answer: The loan can change when the parties amend it or the borrower exercises an extension. The update reaches your feed on the source’s reporting schedule, and the filer can revise a report later. Keep the effective date and publication date so you can see the lag.

faqs.question: Can I find every commercial mortgage maturity date in public data?
faqs.answer: Publicly filed securitizations and disclosures from public borrowers cover part of the market. Private loans may require records from the lender or servicer. Track which loans have missing dates so they remain visible in portfolio reporting.

sections.heading: Which records show whether megawatt charging has opened?

blocks.text: The Port of Long Beach’s May notice for FM Harbor describes a Megawatt Charging System (MCS) installation with two dispensers. Forum Mobility later reported a November 5 ribbon-cutting and an inaugural charging session. In Colton, a November 19 public notice describes two MCS dispensers as an installation project at an existing charging center. Greenlane’s location page lists its CCS equipment. Record the date and scope of each event and check the operator’s current booking channel for MCS access.

Combined Charging System (CCS) and MCS use different connectors. Match the truck’s inlet to the bay the operator assigns. A fleet that stocks both vehicle types also needs separate rows for connector availability in dispatch.

sections.heading: Will the truck get enough energy during its scheduled stop?

blocks.text: Suppose a tractor pulling a trailer needs 180 kWh added to its battery during a 45-minute stop. Allow 10 minutes to enter, connect and leave. In the remaining 35 minutes the battery needs about 309 kW on average, calculated as 180 ÷ (35 ÷ 60). A 240 kW unit would deliver at most 140 kWh in that window, even at its rated output for the entire session and before losses. At Colton, that points the dispatcher toward a pull-through 400 kW CCS bay for further checks.

A 400 kW rating is a screening input. Ask how much the truck actually accepts over its arrival and departure battery levels, whether the bay shares power, and whether the fleet has a reservation. Include a fallback stop with enough energy to reach it. Recheck any quoted price against the operator’s current fleet terms.

title: How to screen a truck depot with a 5 MW service limit
description: Use truck schedules, parcel access, and utility evidence to screen an EV fleet charging site. A 99-truck example shows when a 5 MW limit can work.
coverAlt: Modeled demand at a truck depot over 24 hours. Charging on arrival peaks at 5.13 MW around 6 p.m. Spreading the same charging energy over parked hours peaks at 1.45 MW.
coverCaption: Illustrative 15-minute demand at the meter using NREL warehouse-delivery operating patterns. Both schedules deliver the same charging energy and include 400 kW of other site demand.
intro: A 5 MW service limit can work for a truck charging depot when enough trucks stay parked long enough. Start with the energy each truck needs before its next dispatch, the time it can stay plugged in, and the load the rest of the site already uses. In our 99-truck example, charging on arrival peaks at 5.13 MW at the meter. Spreading the same energy over parked hours reduces the peak to 1.45 MW. The same 5 MW limit falls short when all trucks have only three hours.
takeaways: Model the busy dispatch day with return times, departure deadlines, required battery energy, and realistic charger limits.
Route a loaded truck to the proposed gate and draw its movement inside the yard. A parcel close to the interstate can still have an unusable entrance.
Ask the serving utility for the meter limit, service date, upgrade scope, and rate for each phase. Compare those terms with the site and truck commitments.

sections.heading: What changes when trucks charge overnight?

blocks.text: We built an example day from 99 single-shift operating patterns published with Brennan Borlaug and colleagues’ 2021 study. Each pattern represents one truck in the example, with its published route mileage and return and departure times. The model repeats that day, rounds each parking window inward to complete 15-minute intervals, and assumes 1.8 kWh per mile at the battery and 92% charging efficiency. Each truck can draw up to 100 kW AC at its port. Other site demand stays at 400 kW. This is a constructed fleet day using published inputs.

rows: Charge on arrival
5.13 MW peak, starting at 6 p.m.
One 15-minute interval exceeds the limit.
Spread charging over each truck’s parked hours
1.45 MW peak with the same 15.83 MWh of charging energy.
The example stays below the limit and supplies each truck’s route energy.
Give all trucks the same three-hour window
A maximum of 13.80 MWh for charging after other site load. The fleet needs 15.83 MWh.
The fleet is short about 2.03 MWh. Four trucks also need more energy than a 100 kW port can deliver in three hours.

blocks.text: The two overnight schedules each assume one working port per truck, constant efficiency, and no battery storage. Vehicle charging power can fall as batteries fill. Late returns, reserve requirements, charger downtime, and shared cabinets can change what is possible. Test those cases with your actual trucks before treating the lower peak as a design input.

sections.heading: Screen a depot parcel near I-35

blocks.text: Pick the interchange your trucks will actually use. In Texas, local truck routes and posted restrictions can change the last mile. Check the route in both directions with the dimensions and loaded weight of your tractor and trailer. Review the driveway and traffic movements with the road authority or local jurisdiction before you rely on a route.

rows: Truck access
Route to the actual gate, turn restrictions, clearances, posted bridge limits, approach grade, and space to queue without blocking the road.
Usable yard
Parcel and survey, swept paths for a loaded truck, parking and trailer movements, charger cable reach, and areas needed for maintenance and emergency access.
Land and approvals
Documented site control, zoning and use permissions, drainage and flood screening, access and construction rights, and the easements required for service.
Utility service
Named utility and delivery point, current interval demand, proposed incremental and total import by phase, energization milestones, dependencies, and project cost responsibility.
Backup charging
An accessible station with a compatible connector and enough room for the fleet’s vehicles. Confirm access, operating hours, current port availability, and fallback terms with the operator.

blocks.text: Advance a parcel when the truck path, concept layout, and service path can all support the same dispatch plan. A parcel whose only workable gate sends tractor-trailers across a weight-restricted bridge stays off the shortlist until there is a documented alternate route. A parcel with good access and a utility date after the planned truck delivery needs a phased fleet plan or a different site.

sections.heading: Which data and APIs answer which questions?

rows: How much energy is needed before dispatch?
Fleet telematics, dispatch logs, and vehicle specifications. The national lab’s EVI-X tools support fleet and charging analysis.
Use arrival time, next departure, state of charge and usable battery capacity. Check charger-to-vehicle compatibility and how power changes during a session.
Can the truck reach the parcel?
A truck-routing API such as ArcGIS, together with state and local route restrictions.
Set the right truck dimensions and route to the actual gate. Confirm posted and private restrictions, then review the turns on the site plan.
Is a backup charger usable?
DOE’s Alternative Fueling Station Locator tracks station status, access, connectors, and maximum vehicle class where available.
Check the date and confirm with the operator. A listed vehicle class describes physical access. It cannot establish the current wait time, reserved capacity, or access rights.
What can I learn about the parcel and nearby infrastructure?
Invariant Earth’s catalog lists parcel, terrain, floodplain, and nearby grid-asset fields.
Retain the source, vintage and field status. Use them to eliminate or prioritize parcels and take the proposed load to the serving utility.

sections.heading: What to send the utility before you sign a lease

blocks.text: Send the parcel and proposed service location, fleet and port counts by phase, the requested service dates, and a busy-day load profile showing both charging and other site demand. Identify the charge-management limit you can enforce and explain how the fleet will operate when a charger is down or a shift gets back late. Ask which study and agreements are required, which upgrades or easements are on the critical path, and what deposits or construction costs the customer would carry.

Ask for the applicable tariff and the meter’s billing rules, including demand charges and time-of-use periods. A lower modeled peak helps evaluate the design. Your business case also depends on energy delivered, the rate and any contractual obligations. For a candidate with an existing service, confirm which load and delivery date the utility can support for your phase and configuration.

faqs.question: How many 100 kW chargers fit within a 5 MW meter limit?
faqs.answer: With 400 kW of other site demand, 4.6 MW remains. That supports 46 concurrent 100 kW AC draws in the simple example. The number of trucks the site can serve over a day also depends on parking time, dispatch deadlines, per-vehicle energy, and shared equipment.

faqs.question: Does a nearby substation tell me whether the depot can get 5 MW?
faqs.answer: A nearby substation helps identify where to ask about service. Confirm the actual connection point, available service by phase, required work, and delivery date with the serving utility.

faqs.question: What should I send with an EV fleet charging site inquiry?
faqs.answer: Send the parcel or gate coordinate, the truck and trailer dimensions, the return and departure schedule, energy needed before each dispatch, existing site load, requested phase limits and dates, and any minimum operating requirements during charger outages.

title: Regrid Alternatives for U.S. Parcel Data APIs
description: Compare Regrid, LightBox, Realie, Korzy and other parcel APIs. Download a six-case scorecard for condo lots, parcel splits, and mergers.
coverAlt: Aerial view of Midtown Manhattan with the Digital Tax Map base lot for 432 Park Avenue outlined in gold.
coverCaption: 432 Park Avenue. The outline shows the Digital Tax Map base lot. Aerial imagery from NYS ITS, 2024. The individual commercial unit does not have its own polygon in the queried tax-map layer.
intro: Use Invariant Earth when the parcel needs to be evaluated against terrain, hazards and infrastructure. Compare Regrid and LightBox for parcel boundaries, Realie and ATTOM for assessor-linked property records, and Korzy and Mireye for site context. Start with the same county records for every vendor. Our test at 432 Park Avenue found three tax IDs at one address, two almost identical outlines, and a commercial unit without a polygon in the queried layer.
takeaways: Use the same six inputs for each provider. Keep the county identifier, the provider identifier and the entity each one represents.
Record whether a returned shape belongs to the requested unit, a parent lot or another match.
Test a parcel split and merger. An unchanged parcel ID can still refer to a different boundary after the change.

sections.heading: Compare parcel APIs by the job you need to do

blocks.text: The comparison uses public product documentation checked on November 22, 2026. Invariant makes Invariant Earth. The independent reference below comes from New York City records. Use the scorecard to test each product on the plan you would buy.

rows: Regrid
Parcel GeoJSON by address, assessor number, or spatial query, with a provider ID and documented refresh rules.
Compare an exact assessor-number lookup with an address result. Check stacked parcels and what happens to the ID after a split.
LightBox
Parcel boundaries and links to related assessment and property records using LightBox IDs.
Check which assessment record and building the parcel links to. Check whether the billing and unit records remain distinct.
Realie
A property API with parcel ID, address and spatial searches, assessor data and parcel boundaries.
Run a condo lookup with and without a unit number. Record each tax ID and determine which entity the returned geometry describes.
ATTOM
Property profiles with assessor identifiers, tax, transaction, and other property attributes. Boundary products are documented separately.
Confirm that the product includes the geometry you need and that you can join it to the right tax record.
West Kite
Commercial property research with parcel records, owners, assessments, and other records where available by county.
Test the relevant county fields and whether the API can return the parent and unit under their own identifiers.
Korzy
Address or point lookup with intersecting parcels, optional shape, nearby infrastructure, and coverage status.
Capture all parcels covering the point. Compare the returned local and provider IDs and check which fields are unknown or lack coverage.
Mireye
Cited geospatial enrichment for a selected parcel from an address or coordinate, with additional site data.
Inspect which parcel the address or coordinate matched. Test how it reports the unit, parent geometry, and source of each field.
Invariant Earth
Coordinate-based parcel matching and field-level data for parcel, terrain, hazards, and nearby infrastructure.
Check match type, distance and field status. Invariant Earth identifies its parcel ID as Regrid’s, so use the county records for an independent boundary check.

blocks.text: Paxiv offers parcel and zoning research in a hosted workspace and documents API and MCP access for agent workflows. Scout Data offers a property lookup API geared toward homeowner research, including permit signals and contact data. When the application requires geometry or historical tax lots, ask for a sample of those specific records and the terms that cover their use.

sections.heading: Three tax lot IDs at one Manhattan address

blocks.text: At 432 Park Avenue, Manhattan condo number 2352 links two different lot identifiers. NYC Finance’s Digital Tax Map stores the base lot under 1012920033. NYC Planning’s MapPLUTO uses billing lot 1012927502. NYC Finance separately records the commercial club as unit lot 1012921303. Each number is a borough, block, and lot identifier, commonly called a BBL.

rows: Digital Tax Map base lot
The mapped parent land polygon.
MapPLUTO billing lot
A mapped polygon under the billing ID, with over 99.99% area overlap with the base polygon.
Commercial condominium unit
A separate unit tax record. An exact lookup in the Digital Tax Map polygon layer returned zero polygons.

blocks.text: We joined the condominium table by its billing BBL, checked the unit’s link to the same base lot, and compared the two published shapes in the New York Long Island State Plane coordinate system. The overlap is the area of the intersection divided by the area of the union. MapPLUTO’s documentation explains why the names differ. The city uses the Digital Tax Map base geometry to represent the billing lot and can combine several base lots for some complexes.

A parcel-level map can show the mapped parent for a site screen. A unit-level ownership or tax lookup needs the unit record and its own source. An API that displays the parent shape on a unit lookup should label that relationship explicitly. Counting both outlines here as separate pieces of land would count almost the same area twice.

faqs.question: What are good alternatives to Regrid for parcel data?
faqs.answer: Compare LightBox for boundaries linked to assessments and structures, Realie for assessor-linked property lookups, and Korzy or Mireye for parcel and site context. Test each against the authoritative records for the counties you need.

faqs.question: Does a condo unit tax lot always have its own parcel polygon?
faqs.answer: The answer depends on what the jurisdiction publishes. At 432 Park Avenue, the commercial unit has its own BBL in the condominium unit table. The queried Digital Tax Map polygon layer returns no polygon for that BBL. The parent lot geometry is available separately.

faqs.question: Is Invariant Earth an independent source for Regrid parcel data?

title: Solar farm site selection with GIS and interconnection data
description: Screen buildable acres, compare points of interconnection, and verify solar export capacity. See what changed between two PJM study phases at one substation.
coverAlt: Chart of PJM allocated interconnection cost estimates at Nottingham 138 kV. The original request rose from $2.33 million to $4.16 million. Its 200 MW uprate rose from $2.68 million to $6.34 million.
coverCaption: PJM Transition Cycle 2 estimates at Nottingham 138 kV, Ohio. The chart compares allocations published in October 2025 and June 2026.
intro: Before you option land for a utility-scale solar farm, check whether the tract fits the proposed array and whether the grid can take the project’s output on your schedule. Use GIS to calculate contiguous buildable acreage and map routes to candidate connections. Then verify the exact point of interconnection, requested export in MW AC, upgrade costs, and schedule against the operator’s studies and project agreement.
takeaways: Keep the buildable polygons, the exclusions that produced them, and the largest contiguous area. The acreage on an assessor record cannot tell you what fits.
Use line and substation maps to find connection candidates. Verify the terminal or line tap, the route from the project, and the export case with the transmission provider.
Carry forward the latest study version and scope. At one Ohio substation, the estimate for a 200 MW solar uprate went from $2.68 million to $6.34 million between PJM study phases.

sections.heading: Calculate buildable acres inside the land you can control

blocks.text: Start with the surveyed or cadastral boundary and the parcels you can actually assemble. Mark gaps, easements, and access you would need across other land. Set a preliminary slope and grading tolerance with the layout engineer. Keep terrain, mapped wetlands, flood hazards, setbacks, and permit constraints as separate layers so the team can see and revise each assumption.

rows: Land and site control
County parcel GIS, assessor records, recorded plats and easements, and the current local siting rules.
Parcel IDs and boundaries, control dates, known easements, and the jurisdiction responsible for each approval.
Slope and grading
USGS 3DEP elevation. Choose the best available resolution for the site and check it against a survey before design.
Slope raster, elevation resolution and vintage, the assumed slope limits, and areas that need a grading check.
Water and hazards
U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service wetland mapping and FEMA’s National Flood Hazard Layer.
Mapped wetland and flood polygons, map dates, any screening buffers, and areas to verify in the field.
Solar resource and layout
National Solar Radiation Database weather and irradiance, a preliminary array layout, and site access plans.
Resource dataset and weather years, MW DC, inverter MW AC, usable blocks, and space for roads, drainage, and equipment.
Connection route
Transmission-owner maps and records, local parcel geometry, and the applicable generator interconnection queue.
Candidate connection, likely transmission owner, plausible lead-line route, and the parcels or rights of way the route crosses.

blocks.text: Intersect each exclusion with the tract, merge the overlapping exclusions, and subtract their combined area using a local projected coordinate system suited to measuring acreage. Say a 960-acre tract has 150 acres above your slope limit and 120 acres in a preliminary wetland exclusion, with 45 acres that satisfy both. The combined exclusion is 225 acres, leaving 735 acres for further screening. A layout with a largest contiguous block of 410 acres has a different design problem from a single 735-acre block. These numbers are illustrative. Keep each disconnected block, then test roads, drainage, equipment, and grading on the layout.

sections.heading: What establishes solar export capacity at a substation?

blocks.text: A transmission map can show that a line crosses the property. A queue can show who has applied and what the operator has published about those applications. To underwrite export, identify the exact connection and ask the operator which service, study assumptions, upgrades, and operating limits apply to your request. Ask for the date of the evidence and any conditions on construction and operation.

items: Record the proposed export at the connection in MW AC. Track panel nameplate in MW DC and inverter rating separately. For co-located batteries, also specify import, discharge, plant controls, and which resources can operate at the same time.
Name the substation bus or line tap, voltage, transmission owner, and proposed generator lead. Trace a viable route and identify crossings or easements that could delay it.

Check the operator’s queue and study versions by request ID. Capture earlier requests the study depends on, other affected transmission systems, required upgrades, cost allocation, and who is responsible for building what.

Get the latest applicable study, agreement, and upgrade schedule before treating an export assumption as committed. Confirm the applicable operating limits, milestones, and deliverability terms with the operator.

blocks.text: The public queue is useful when an option period is short. It can help focus questions and reveal competing or dependent requests. Each entry has a status and a reporting date. A withdrawn project’s requested MW cannot be treated as capacity available to your tract. For distribution-connected projects, start with the serving utility and its applicable process.

sections.heading: At Nottingham 138 kV, the same uprate got a higher estimate

blocks.text: PJM studied two linked requests from Energy Pastures Solar Project in Harrison County, Ohio. AG2-082 was the original 200 MW request. AH1-580 requested a 200 MW increase at the same point of interconnection. The 400 MW maximum facility output on the AH1-580 report includes the original 200 MW. Adding that 400 MW to the original 200 MW would count the original request twice.

rows: AG2-082 · original 200 MW
AH1-580 · 200 MW uprate

blocks.text: The uprate still requested 200 MW of energy service in Phase II. Its allocated physical network upgrade line increased from $2.326 million to $4.575 million, and the new estimate included $609,937 for transmission-owner interconnection facilities. Phase I had recorded zero on that facilities line and said that the physical facilities study would begin in Phase II. Carry the scope and stage beside the number. A zero from an earlier study may describe what has been priced so far.

We used the project allocation total as printed in each report. Those totals are estimates for those requests. The Phase II reports used a 2028 model base case. A separate agreement and project schedule would establish rights and milestones. The study figures cannot establish remaining capacity for a new applicant at Nottingham.

sections.heading: Which GIS tools and APIs fit a solar developer’s workflow?

blocks.text: Use public GIS layers when you need to run your own polygon calculations. PVcase Prospect documents a greenfield workflow for filtering by buildable acres and working with site constraints. Geoforge’s example report shows how a separate power screen can organize modeled headroom, queue records, and upgrades. Ask each provider which cases it covers and which results you can export with dates and sources.

Invariant Earth publishes fields for elevation, slope, wetland and flood indicators, and distance to transmission lines and substations. Use point fields to enrich a search, then use the tract and layout polygons to calculate buildable acreage. When evaluating an API, ask for the original source and geometry, the units, and the behavior when data is missing. Invariant publishes this guide. We checked the listed capabilities against public documentation.

A useful shortlist lets the next reviewer recreate the decision. Save the parcel and buildable geometry, the assumed project layout, and one record per candidate connection. Give each record a source, date, proposed MW, study stage, estimated upgrades, and open items. Before a land option goes hard, assign a person and due date to the evidence that could change your decision.

faqs.question: Can I estimate buildable solar acres from parcel data?
faqs.answer: Use the parcel boundary as the starting geometry. Subtract the union of exclusions and project setbacks, then keep both the total remaining area and the contiguous blocks. Check the preliminary result against site control, a layout, local requirements, and field surveys.

faqs.question: Does a nearby power line mean a solar farm can connect?
faqs.answer: A nearby power line gives you a candidate to investigate. Confirm the actual connection configuration, who owns the line, how the project can reach it, and whether the operator’s study supports the requested export under its modeled conditions.

faqs.question: Why are the PJM MW Energy and MW Capacity fields different?
faqs.answer: PJM reports the MW in the energy request separately from the MW it recognizes as Capacity in the study. AH1-580 lists a 200 MW energy request and a 134 MW Capacity increase. Its 400 MW maximum facility output refers to the combined facility after the proposed uprate.

title: Battery storage site selection for charging and discharge
description: Screen utility-scale battery sites for import and export MW, usable charging hours, queue dependencies, and grid upgrades. Compare three public studies.
coverAlt: Illustrative chart at a 50 MW import limit and 90% round-trip efficiency. Eight hours of charging supports 360 MWh of export and leaves a 40 MWh shortfall. Nine hours supports the 400 MWh target.
coverCaption: Illustrative recharge screen at the point of interconnection. A 50 MW import cap gives very different results when the battery can charge for eight hours or nine.
intro: A utility-scale battery energy storage system (BESS) needs a connection that can take power from the grid when the project plans to charge and deliver power back when it plans to discharge. Screen those two directions separately. Record the point of interconnection, the allowed hours and operating conditions for each direction, and the upgrades and dates that apply. Then check whether the permitted charging window can refill enough energy for the discharge you plan to sell.
takeaways: Ask the operator for maximum net import and export in MW at the same connection point, with dates, operating limits, and the documents behind both values.
A 100 MW battery that needs to deliver 400 MWh takes nearly nine hours to refill from empty at a 50 MW import cap and 90% meter-to-meter efficiency.

Keep MW, MWh, and service rights separate in the site record. The report for a 55 MW Virginia battery indicates grid charging in its project summary and leaves the numeric import limit unresolved at that level.

sections.heading: What should a utility-scale battery site screen include?

blocks.text: Start with the operating plan. State the planned discharge in MW, how many hours it must last, the energy available at the meter in MWh, and which hours the project needs to recharge. Identify the grid connection so both studies refer to the same physical point. If solar shares the connection, specify whether the battery can charge from the solar array, the grid, or both. Include the maximum simultaneous net export from the entire site.

rows: Charge from the grid
Net import MW, import hours by season, limits during peak load or outages, and any restrictions on grid charging.
Charging cases and operating assumptions, with the applicable service or agreement terms from the operator.
Discharge to the grid
Net export MW, usable MWh at the meter, export duration, applicable curtailment, and commercial service requested.
Export cases and agreement, including the limits at the proposed point of interconnection and any deliverability terms.
Check the queue and upgrades
Shared connection point, earlier requests the study depends on, upgrade owner, cost allocation, and the date each upgrade is needed.
The operator’s queue and dated study revisions, facilities scope, and schedule for construction and energization.
Check land and access
Controlled acreage, equipment and access layout, flood and drainage constraints, fire access and spacing, and the route of the lead line.
A layout tied to the actual parcels, local planning and fire requirements, and the easements needed for the route.

blocks.text: FERC’s Order No. 2023 directs U.S. transmission providers using the applicable procedures to study storage with assumptions that reflect proposed charging behavior, subject to reliability and good utility practice. Ask the provider which tariff and process apply to the particular connection and whether you need separate charging service. Capture the actual hours, limits, and conditions in the documents that will govern operation.

sections.heading: Three public studies show three kinds of charging evidence

rows: Tupelo Storage · Virginia · PJM 2026
55 MW maximum facility output and 220 MWh battery specification.
The project summary says grid charging is planned. The summary gives no numeric import MW.
Ask for the charging case and import terms. PJM’s Phase II cost summary allocates an estimated $7.64 million to this request.
Deka Road · Pennsylvania · PJM 2011
3 MW studied injection. PJM recognized zero MW as Capacity in the study and described the export as curtailable for reliability.
3.6 MW studied load at the same existing 69 kV connection.
The two directional values differ. Preserve the connection arrangement and the study’s stated treatment of export.
Oneida Energy Storage · Ontario · IESO 2022
250 MW injection evaluated in the study scope. The stated project rating was 250 MW and 1,000 MWh.
250 MW withdrawal evaluated in the same assessment.
Conditional approval carried connection requirements. Certain outage conditions limited the equipment’s ability to provide maximum active power alongside required reactive power.

blocks.text: At Oneida, the grid operator required reactive power capability equal to 33% of rated active power at the transformer terminals. It found 28.4% under the typical voltage condition it assessed at maximum injection. Reactive power helps control voltage and affects how much equipment capacity remains for active power. The assessment required the applicant to address that shortfall. Oneida later reported starting commercial operation in May 2025. The study figures above describe the proposed project and study conditions in 2022.

The practical test for a new site is to ask which limits already apply, which depend on planned equipment, and which conditions would reduce either direction. For queue records, save the project ID, resource type, stage, related requests, study date, and document URL. For an upgrade, keep the cost estimate vintages and responsibility for construction beside the expected service date.

sections.heading: Can a 50 MW import limit refill a 100 MW battery overnight?

blocks.text: Consider two illustrative battery sites that each need to export 100 MW for four hours and can import up to 50 MW when charging is permitted. Assume 400 MWh of usable export energy, an empty usable energy window at the start, and a constant 90% round-trip efficiency measured at the connection point. To calculate the export energy the charging window can support, multiply 50 MW by the allowed hours and 0.90, up to the battery’s 400 MWh usable limit.

blocks.text: The battery needs about 444 MWh of grid energy and 8 hours, 53 minutes, and 20 seconds at full import to refill from empty. Nine hours leaves little margin. Check the allowed hours against seasonal restrictions, the state of charge at the start of each dispatch cycle, and end-of-life usable capacity. A commercial model should also account for charge ramp, losses across operating conditions, and which hours have power available at an acceptable price.

sections.heading: How to compare candidate battery sites before signing an option

blocks.text: Use parcel boundaries, terrain, flood layers, and transmission maps to check the land and map viable connection routes. Use the operator’s queue and studies at each proposed point to identify other projects and upgrades. A substation distance field is useful for finding candidates. A dated charge and discharge case is what helps the team compare two sites with similar distances.

Send the same operating request for each candidate. State the MW and MWh at the meter, the charging schedule, the expected start date, and how operation changes under outages. Ask the operator to return the cases and documents behind each answer, the earliest date each direction can operate, and the cost and schedule of shared or assigned upgrades. Keep unknown values visible in the shortlist so a reviewer can tell where the investment case relies on unverified service.

faqs.question: Does a 100 MW battery always need 100 MW of charging capacity?
faqs.answer: Charge MW depends on how much energy the battery needs to restore and how long it can charge. A 400 MWh export target with 90% round-trip efficiency needs about 444 MWh of imported energy from empty. At 50 MW, that requires nearly nine hours at full import.

faqs.question: Can a generator interconnection queue tell me how much a battery can charge?
faqs.answer: A queue may list the battery’s size, resource type, and application status. Look for separate numeric import MW and operating conditions in the project’s study and applicable service documents. Some study summaries identify grid charging without stating the allowed import MW.

faqs.question: How do I compare a standalone battery with solar plus storage?
faqs.answer: Compare net import and simultaneous net export at the same point of interconnection. For a hybrid, specify whether the battery can charge from the grid and how the controls share the connection with solar. Document the operating limits the provider actually studied and the conditions attached to any agreement.

title: Retail site selection APIs for trade areas and foot traffic
description: Compare retail locations with travel-time areas, dated store openings, and comparable visit counts. A Harlem case shows how to use public transit data.
coverAlt: Aerial map of two 125th Street subway complexes and Trader Joe’s Harlem. From September 2023 to September 2024, estimated A, B, C and D station entries rose 17.6 percent, and 2 and 3 station entries rose 18.0 percent.
coverCaption: Transit context on 125th Street in Harlem. Station points and entry estimates from the MTA. Store location from NYC GeoSearch. Aerial imagery from NYS ITS Geospatial Services, 2024.
intro: Start in Invariant Earth to check the parcel, building characteristics and road context at a proposed store location. Then connect the site to routing, store history and visits to compare trade areas. Before signing a retail lease, find out who can reach the site, where customers at comparable stores actually come from, and what happened as nearby stores opened or closed. Those questions call for different data. Use routing for travel-time areas, a dated place directory for nearby stores, and comparable visit or pedestrian counts for activity. Keep the area, measure, and time window with every number so you can rerun the comparison.
takeaways: Draw candidate areas using the same travel mode and time. For existing stores, use visitor origins to learn where customers may actually come from.
Confirm openings and closures with dated retailer, landlord, or local records. A database creation date records when the entry appeared in that system.

At two 125th Street subway complexes in Harlem, entries grew about 18% between September 2023 and September 2024. Both are public measures of transit activity. They cannot tell you how many people visited the grocery store that opened nearby.

sections.heading: Which APIs answer each retail site question?

rows: What is at this proposed store location?
Invariant Earth parcel, building and road fields in one coordinate lookup.
Verify the property match and the actual entrance. Use a routing or visit dataset for customer travel and activity.
Who can reach the site in ten minutes?
Esri routing service areas for walking or driving. Use Census ACS estimates to describe households within a defined area.
Use the actual customer entrance, travel mode, network vintage, and time-of-day assumptions. Ask how the provider assigns partially overlapping Census areas and shows uncertainty.
Where do people who visit a comparable store come from?
Placer’s Trade Area report for estimated visitor origins. Its glossary distinguishes visits, unique visitors, and the sampled device panel.
Request the store-level boundary and date range. Check how repeat trips are counted, what is suppressed, and which histories can be regenerated with a common model.
Which nearby stores opened or closed?
Foursquare Open Source Places for location identity and dated releases. Verify events with dated first-party or public records.
Match brand, address, unit, and coordinates. Keep the date the place entered the dataset and the verified operating date as separate fields.
How busy is the corridor at comparable times?
Municipal pedestrian counts or transit agency data. NYC DOT counts pedestrians at sampled locations and the MTA publishes station entry estimates.

Require a defined entrance, count line or property boundary. Preserve hours, days, and the instrument’s definition. For a specific storefront, ask for a comparable venue visit series or a direct count.

blocks.text: For a new site, estimate the reachable area from its entrance and compare it with existing stores of the same format. For an operating store, a share of visits can be traced to aggregate origin areas if the provider offers that report. The network polygon estimates access. The visitor-origin polygon describes where an observed or estimated customer base comes from. Keep both geometries if your team uses both.

sections.heading: What changed near two Harlem locations?

blocks.text: Trader Joe’s opened on West 125th Street in Harlem in July 2024. The National Urban League recorded the announcement that month, and the retailer lists the store at 123 West 125th Street. We used MTA station IDs to match two complexes along the corridor across years. The store address was geocoded through NYC GeoSearch. The comparison uses the station complexes as two observations and keeps the store as a separate record.

Each number represents estimated entries to a subway complex in that month. The MTA includes qualifying free transfers from outside the complex in the entry total, so adding the transfers field again would double count them. We use September in all four years to hold the month and its length constant. The weekday and weekend mix can still differ.

Both complexes grew at nearly the same percentage rate in the first comparison, even though one serves a different set of lines farther west. In the following year the A/B/C/D complex rose about 1.2%, while the 2/3 complex rose about 11.5%. The similarity in year one and divergence in year two show why it helps to look beyond a single station and a single period. An impact estimate for the store would require comparable venue visits or direct counts and a separate analysis of what else changed.

sections.heading: Build a store history you can compare across markets

blocks.text: Create a stable store identity for each location and link it to the lease unit and parcel. When a competitor moves, keep the old site record and the new site record with their respective dates. Save the source and observation time each time you see a change. For an opening, use the best documented public operating date and retain the actual precision, whether it’s a day, a month, or a range.

For visit trends, use the same source and venue boundary for each period. Match operating hours and the weekday and weekend mix where possible. Record holidays, construction, closures, and changes in sampling. For a store inside a mall, test whether the provider measures the store, the common corridor, or the entire property. Ask whether low sample counts are marked or withheld and whether the provider can reproduce an older estimate.

For household and demographic change, use comparable Census geographies and nonoverlapping ACS five-year periods, and keep the margins of error. Those estimates describe people and households in an area. To calculate sales conversion, use store visits and transactions measured for the same doors, dates, and hours.

sections.heading: What to ask for in a vendor trial

blocks.text: Give each provider three sites where you know something about what happened. Choose a standalone location, a store within a larger property, and a competitor that recently moved. Ask for an export with the store identity, the mapped boundary, the date and definition of each observation, and the results for the same two periods. Check the latest result against a dated store listing or your own counts. Test how the provider handles the old location after a move.

Invariant Earth publishes parcel, building, and road context fields for coordinate-based screening. You can use those fields to help resolve the property, then join a routing, visit, or place history product using its appropriate geometry. Invariant publishes this guide. The provider comparison uses public documentation. The Harlem calculation uses open MTA records and does not rely on a commercial visitor estimate.

faqs.question: How can I verify a store opening date from places data?
faqs.answer: Use the place record to locate the store and resolve the brand, address and unit. Confirm the operating date with a dated announcement or local evidence. A database creation date usually describes when the location entered that dataset.

title: Environmental permits and enforcement by parcel
description: Link an industrial parcel to EPA facility IDs and state permits. A Brooklyn case shows why address and boundary searches can miss regulatory records.
coverAlt: Aerial map of Newtown Creek in Brooklyn with tax lot 3025250001 outlined. Two EPA waste-program points sit outside the southern boundary. Five of seven ECHO points tested were covered by the mapped parcel.
coverCaption: Newtown Creek, Brooklyn. The green outline is MapPLUTO tax lot 3025250001, the green dot is the EPA registry point, and the gold dots are the two linked waste-program points outside the lot. Aerial imagery from NYS ITS Geospatial Services, 2024.
intro: To find environmental permits and enforcement history for an industrial site, start with the tax parcel and the operator’s names and addresses. Link those to the EPA Facility Registry Service ID and each program’s permit or handler ID. Search EPA ECHO for dated compliance and enforcement records, then obtain the controlling permits and orders from the issuing agencies. This gives you a record you can review before an acquisition, lease, or expansion.
takeaways: Keep the tax lot, physical facility, regulated operator, and individual program identifiers as distinct records. A facility can use several addresses and share its site with other operators.
At Newtown Creek in Brooklyn, a boundary-only search would miss two of seven coordinate-bearing EPA records already linked to the facility.
Keep the observation date and document status with each result. A compliance status, a later notice, and a draft permit answer different questions.

sections.heading: Where to find industrial permit and enforcement records

rows: What property is in the transaction?
County or city cadastral GIS and assessor records. Use the survey, lease, and property documents for the actual area under review.
Parcel ID, boundary and version, site address aliases, operator names, and the relationship between the owned or leased area and the facility.
Which regulatory programs list the facility?
EPA Facility Registry Service and the program links in ECHO. Search the state’s permit inventory as well.
The EPA registry ID and separate air, water, and waste identifiers with their operator, site address, and reference-point description.
What does the permit allow or require?
The issuing agency’s final permit and modifications. In New York, start with the Department of Environmental Conservation’s permit and map indexes.
Permit type, the effective version and dates, authorized activities or units, applicability, and any conditions that matter to the planned use.
What enforcement or cleanup records exist?
EPA ECHO for program-specific notices, inspection summaries, and actions. Check the issuing agency for the original documents. Check state cleanup and federal Superfund records separately.
Program, event type, case ID and date, disposition where documented, and the geography or activity the record covers.

blocks.text: Use coordinates to find candidate matches. Verify a match with other fields such as program identifiers, address aliases, and the operator on the source document. Keep the original identifiers even when you display one facility. For a campus or a multi-tenant property, check which facility areas or units each document actually covers.

sections.heading: Newtown Creek shows what a boundary-only search misses

blocks.text: NYC GeoSearch returned borough-block-lot 3025250001 for 329 Greenpoint Avenue. MapPLUTO 26v2 lists that lot at 327 Greenpoint Avenue. A 2004 New York State DEC ruling lists the Newtown Creek plant at 329–69 Greenpoint Avenue and pairs DEC facility ID 2-6101-00025 with water permit NY0026204. Looking up that permit in EPA ECHO returns registry ID 110000561268, whose street address is 301 Greenpoint Avenue.

rows: NYC tax lot
MapPLUTO 26v2 provides the boundary. Its address and the GeoSearch address differ.
EPA facility registry
The registry point falls inside the lot. ECHO lists a calculated location accuracy of 372 meters for that point.

description: Find the water and sewer utilities for a property. Compare service area APIs, plant capacity and written allocations using a documented Maryland site.

intro: Use Invariant Earth to screen the parcel against EPA drinking-water and sewer service boundaries. Check the returned source for each layer, then ask the mapped utility to confirm how it would serve the project. Start with the parcel and the local water and sewer service maps. EPA drinking-water boundaries can help identify a system, and EPA wastewater records can identify a treatment plant and its permit. For a project, ask the utility for written confirmation of the volumes, connection points and delivery dates it can support. A service-area map answers where to ask. The written allocation and service conditions determine what the site can use.
takeaways: Match water and sewer separately. Keep the source, mapped classification and date for both.
An empty EPA overlap can occur where a local plan already shows future service. Check the local record before ruling out the site.
Keep the project’s maximum-day water allocation separate from annual consumption, plant-wide wastewater capacity and the site’s permitted sewer discharge.

blocks.text: The January 2026 site-plan staff packet lists the Aligned project at 5601 Manor Woods Road, Tax Map 94, Parcel 71, Lot 106. Frederick County Water Resources Element
